Title: Postdoc in Multi-Modal Behavioural Modelling - DTU Compute
Place: Kongens Lyngby, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
Description:
Job Description

If you are looking to establish yourself as a researcher in the cross-disciplinary fields of machine learning and mental health, this postdoc position is for you.

At DTU Compute you will focus is on building multi modal models for mental health applications in a Danish context. You will collaborate with a mental health department at the hospital (Region H), startup companies, as well as Denmark’s AI research and development house, Alexandra Instituttet. Our joint grand solution project is providing foundational models (wearables, speech, video) for behavioural modelling across several mental health applications.

Responsibilities And Qualifications

As part of the position, you will be responsible for:


Data collection activities
Data annotation activities
Developing novel models for multi modalities, herein wearables, speech, and/or video
Pursuing the aims of making foundation models more representative.
Modelling data from mental health applications in collaboration with mental health experts
Conducting computational research experiments and disseminating these in research papers
Good collaborations with project partners (incl. hospitals and companies)


We are looking for you with


Outstanding interdisciplinary collaboration skills
Good organizational/project management skills
Excellent research skills in machine learning and an
Interest in mental health applications


As a formal qualification, you must hold a PhD degree (or equivalent).

We offer

DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and terms of employment

The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. In addition, supplements can be negotiated in accordance with DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures .

The period of employment is 22 months. Start date is according to mutual agreement. The position is a full-time position.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here .

Further information

Further information may be obtained from Line Clemmensen, Lkhc@dtu.dk .

You can read more about DTU Compute at www.compute.dtu.dk .

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark .

Application procedure

Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 12 October 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:


Application (cover letter)
CV
Academic Diplomas (MSc/PhD – in English)
List of publications


Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Compute – Department of Applied Mathematics and Computer Science – is an internationally recognised academic environment with over 400 employees and 10 research sections. We broadly cover digital technologies within mathematics, data science, computer science, and computer engineering, including artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, internet of things (IoT), chip design, cybersecurity, human-computer interaction, social networks, fairness, and data ethics. Our research is rooted in basic research and centres on mathematical models of the physical and virtual world, as a basis for the analysis, design, and implementation of complex systems. We focus on ensuring that our research results contribute to creating a better society by supporting areas such as health, green transition, energy supply, and life science. We collaborate with universities, public and private organisations, and companies in Denmark and abroad, and through DTU’s startup ecosystem, we encourage innovation and entrepreneurship. We have a strong ethical, human, and sustainable approach that ensures integrity in our work. Therefore, we strive for and take responsibility for driving the democratisation of digital technologies, so that everyone has the opportunity to actively participate in the development, and we ensure a continued open, democratic, and inclusive society for the benefit of all. At DTU Compute, we value diversity, inclusion, and a flexible work-life balance. Read more here: www.compute.dtu.dk .

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829

DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

Title: Machine Learning Engineer
Place: Copenhagen, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
Description:
Veo is an AI-powered sports camera and analysis ecosystem built for one job: turning what happens on a pitch into proof. Capture, viewing, data and analytics, sharing- all in one system, all pointed at the same thing.

That's bigger than football. Every player, on every pitch, gets access to the kind of proof only the top academies used to keep for themselves. It's the future we're building.

Every youth match still has a moment nobody saw. A run that won the game, underneath everyone's radar. A kid written off before anyone actually checked. We exist to close that gap, one match at a time.

One camera on any pitch feeds an AI that tracks every player and the ball for the whole game, turning what happened into evidence instead of somebody's opinion.

That's the actual job here. Not shipping features. Building the system that gives proof to someone who used to rely on a hunch.

If you've ever watched a match and wondered who else saw what you saw, you already know why this matters.

We're looking for people who want to build that future with us.

As a Machine Learning Engineer at Veo you will get to work on challenging problems and directly contribute to the value created by our AI-driven end-user products.

You will become part of our AI team, which comprises 20+ researchers and engineers responsible for all stages in the machine learning lifecycles across different projects - from scoping and defining data annotation tasks to modeling, validation, and deployment. You will be free to determine the directions of the project you work on while also getting feedback and being encouraged to spar with the rest of the team to assist each other in improving and succeeding.

We stay current with the latest research and continuously discuss concepts and ideas in recent papers to assess their relevance to our tasks and product-specific challenges.

We are looking to add yet another ambitious, high-performing junior to mid-level engineer or/researcher with proven experience from real-world machine learning projects to the team. Experience with computer vision is advantageous but not a must.

What you will do:



Train state-of-the-art machine learning models
Write efficient inference pipelines for cloud and edge
Define and supervise data annotation tasks
Improve evaluation schemes to increase understanding of model performance and shortcomings
Contribute to long-term planning and prioritization of tasks




What you will need:



MSc or PhD in a relevant field
Hands-on experience with real-world, large-scale machine-learning projects
Great coding skills
Skilled at both autonomous tasks and contributing to group efforts
Ability to examine details closely and critically




Our Copenhagen office mirrors our innovative technology – with an indoor ball court, rooftop terrace, and well-equipped gym. We have created a facility that supports connecting disciplines across the business, facilitates creative thinking, and gives the space to engage with colleagues, our global partners, and the entire Veo community.

Values we hold at Veo:

Dare - We take initiative, stay curious, and challenge the status quo in our work.

Own it - We drive impact by identifying opportunities, taking responsibility, and confidently executing.

Level up - We embrace growth, continuously learning and shaping our skills.

Play as a team - We collaborate across a diverse organization, leveraging shared insights for stronger

outcomes.

Customer Centric - We deliver value by having close partnerships and a deep understanding of our customers (internally and externally)

We value diversity and inclusion and welcome applicants from all backgrounds, even if your experience doesn’t completely match every qualification listed. What matters most is your creativity, potential, and ability to make meaningful contributions.

Place: Copenhagen, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
Description:
Building trusted AI-powered analytics for healthcare training outcomes




Make an impact with Laerdal!

Laerdal Medical is a world leader in healthcare education and resuscitation training that uses immersive technologies and data-centric insights to increase survival and improve healthcare quality. Laerdal Copenhagen is our Center of excellence for Digital Learning, and on a global scale, we work with leading life-saving institutions around the world including emergency services, hospitals, ambulance services, first aid organizations, and educational institutions. Our products help these organizations save lives every day. We are a dynamic and energetic organization consisting of people from a wide variety of cultures and backgrounds. Our goal is to help save one million more lives, every year, by 2030, and to do so sustainably.




Position overview

We work in the space of advanced analytics for learners in healthcare and are looking to expand our team. In our area of Resuscitation Quality Improvement (RQI) we serve as the interface for varying roles in the healthcare system that want to know how their learners are doing, where they can improve and how prioritizing a high-quality training curriculum elevates the skills of their workforce.




Our product team spans multiple roles, backgrounds and nationalities and for the next major phase in how we deliver insights to users, we want your help:

Do you understand how to translate a vast structured data foundation into actionable insights for different user groups and metrics?

Do you have experience in advanced analytics, i.e. leveraging LLMs, statistics and ML? Have you implemented agentic systems? Do you know how to move from product idea to trustworthy user-facing feature in this space?

Do you want to help us on our mission to help save (even more) lives?




If you answered YES to those questions, don’t hesitate to apply with a brief personal motivation and CV and we might soon be getting to know each other in person!




What we want to build with you:

AI-Ready data foundation: guaranteeing high data quality for AI, refining the data model and ensuring efficient retrieval/search across our domain
Agentic data analyst: empower our analytics users to uncover individualized insights by combining traditional analytics with agentic workloads.
Operational excellence for AI: continuously learning and adapting the system while collaborating closely with product and design experts on the team




How you will contribute to the team:

Design and implement agentic product features for our custom advanced analytics platform
Understand and improve our domain data model
Partner with the Product Manager and Design Researcher to understand user needs, gather requirements and translate them into technical solutions
Ensure security/compliance and governed access for customers and internal users as well as safe guardrails for AI




Which skills you should bring (AI & data):

Hands-on experience in data modeling, production ready LLM solutions and using tools such as Langchain, Mastra, Embabel or other ADKs
Proficiency in using cloud data platforms and corresponding tools; e.g. PySpark, SQL, Databricks as well as the tools that enable search indexes, RAG or other integration patterns
Proven understanding of different agent workflow patterns and their benefits
(optional) Experience in data governance, semantic models and metadata management




Software engineering & other skills:

Knowledge of engineering practices and willingness to discuss them with peers; e.g. branching strategies, TDD, agile & DevOps principles
Advanced abilities in AI coding: harness engineering, skills development, context engineering, etc.
(optional) Knowledge in IaC tools and cloud solution architecture
(optional) Domain knowledge in healthcare and/or learning systems




Why join Laerdal Copenhagen?

Join a mission-driven team where your work helps improve healthcare and save lives around the world. You'll enjoy a high-trust, low-bureaucracy environment that values autonomy, collaboration, craftsmanship, and continuous learning. Our Copenhagen office, located in a historic warehouse in the city center, combines an ambitious, international culture with a relaxed atmosphere, great colleagues, and flexible working conditions. We are currently counting 160 colleagues in Copenhagen – a mix of talents across engineering, design, learning- and medical specialists, working in cross functional teams. As part of Laerdal Medical, you'll work locally with a talented team while being connected to a global organization of 2,200+ people dedicated to helping save one million more lives, every year, by 2030.




Learn more about our mission: One Million More Lives

Or get a glimpse of our office culture: Laerdal Copenhagen 2022 | Videos & Movies on Vimeo




Interested?

Apply with your CV and a short motivation explaining why this role speaks to you. (Remember, LinkedIn allows only one document, so please merge your CV and motivation letter into one file.)




If you have any questions that might keep you from applying, reach out by e-mail to Engineering Manager Jasper Hahn Jasper.Hahn@laerdal.com.




We’ll review applications and set up interviews on an ongoing basis.

Title: Postdoctoral Researcher in Arctic Sea-Ice and Initialised Climate Prediction
Place: Copenhagen, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
Description:
The Arctic is warming faster than any other region on Earth. DMI is looking for a scientist to uncover how Arctic sea-ice predictability evolves in a warming climate and to pioneer AI-enhanced approaches that advance our ability to predict sea-ice conditions from seasonal to multi-annual timescales.




The Danish Meteorological Institute (DMI) opens a 4-year, full time position for a post doc research scientist in the Danish National Centre for Climate Research (NCKF), to work with AI-facilitated climate predictions of a seasonally ice-free Arctic in the Novo Nordic Foundation project IcyAlert (https://icyalert.github.io/).




IcyAlert (Intelligent Climate Early Warning Alert for Arctic Ice-Free Summers) is a research project funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation (NNF). The project goal is to improve predictions of Arctic ice-free summers and its potential climate impacts at multi-seasonal time scale using global climate models, causal analysis and machine learning. IcyAlert is led by DMI, in partnership with the Royal Meteorological Institute of Belgium (RMI) and the Technical University of Denmark (DTU).




As part of NCKF at DMI, you will work in a research department with a strong profile in both global and regional climate modelling, as well as remote sensing. You will be part of the Global Climate unit in NCKF.




Your main tasks and responsibilities

In the IcyAlert project you will focus on how winter climate states and key physical drivers influence subsequent sea-ice evolution and predictability across seasonal to multi-annual timescales.




Building on causal relationships identified by RMI, you will use probabilistic AI methods to generate targeted initial-condition ensembles for sensitivity experiments.




You will then conduct and analyse both initialised ensemble prediction experiments for Arctic sea ice using the EC-Earth model system (https://ec-earth.org/), which is already running at DMI, to evaluate which winter variables or processes contribute most strongly to subsequent summer sea-ice predictability. The resulting process understanding and datasets will feed back into the ML-based, observation-driven Arctic sea-ice prediction system developed in collaboration with DTU.




You can expect to contribute to climate-impact assessments, including applications related to Arctic navigability. You will lead and co-author scientific publications and will contribute grant applications.




Your qualifications

We are particularly interested in candidates with a strong background in climate prediction, Arctic climate, and/or sea-ice science, as well as experience working with initialised ensemble prediction systems.

Expected qualifications include:




A PhD in climate science, atmospheric science, oceanography, sea-ice science, Earth-system science, applied mathematics, or a closely related field
Experience with initialised climate prediction systems, including ensemble-based forecasts or hindcast evaluation, and in working with large climate datasets
Strong scientific programming skills, particularly in Python, and preferably experience working with HPC environments
Good communication skills in oral and written English and collaboration skills for working with scientists within DMI and across three project partner institutions. The postdoctoral researcher will play a key role in connecting climate dynamics and initialized ensemble prediction (DMI), with causal methods (RMI), and AI/ML-based prediction (DTU). This will help ensure that IcyAlert forecasts are not only skilful but also physically interpretable and dynamically consistent.




Advanced expertise in developing new machine-learning architectures is not required. More important is the ability to physically understand initialised climate predictions, evaluate whether forecast signals are meaningful, and work effectively with AI/ML and causal-analysis methods developed in the IcyAlert project.

Where relevant, the postdoctoral researcher may also contribute to coordinated multi-annual hindcast experiments, such as the CMIP7/DCPP-A protocol, when this aligns with IcyAlert priorities and EC-Earth climate prediction-system development at DMI.




Who are we?

The position is in the Danish National Centre for Climate Research (NCKF) at the Danish Meteorological Institute (DMI), which employs approximately 80 climate scientists of which 25 are located in the Global Climate unit. The companion Centre for Weather Research at DMI employs researchers working with meteorology, oceanography and hydrology. We have a strong international profile, which is also reflected in the many nationalities employed and in the use of both English and Danish as working languages.




NCKF has been established with the purpose to conduct critical climate research for the Kingdom of Denmark (Denmark, Greenland and the Faroe Islands) and bring together climate knowledge, to form the basis for green transition and climate adaptation. The activities include assessments of observed and future climate change of the physical climate system, with focus on the Polar regions and on extreme weather and sea level around Denmark. Across the department, climate research builds on both global and regional modelling as well as observations from remote sensing, in-situ measurements and field work. NCKF also develops the Danish Climate Atlas (Klimaatlas) which contains detailed data about expected future changes in the climate of Denmark.




DMI is part of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Utilities. As of December 1, 2026, DMI will merge with our sister agency, Danish Agency for Climate Data, to become “DMI, Maps and Basic Data”. DMI is the government's climate science advisor, creating and communicating knowledge about weather, climate and the sea to the Danish Realm. DMI's warnings, weather forecasts and services safeguard life and infrastructure and provide a basis for planning in a changing climate. We have approximately 350 employees, most of whom work at DMI’s headquarters at Sankt Kjelds Gård in Østerbro, Copenhagen. After the merge, the new organization will have more than 600 employees. 




Employment and Salary

Will be in accordance with Danish Law and Agreements, specifically the Collective Agreement for State-Employed Academics (AC-overenskomsten). It will be possible to negotiate an addition to the basic salary depending on your qualifications and experience. DMI offers a flexible working week of 37 hours including a paid lunch break, and six weeks of paid vacation annually. If you come from abroad, there is a possibility for a reduced tax scheme the first 7 years in Denmark.




The position is a full-time position, limited to a duration of 4 years.




For further details about the position, please contact the Head of Global Climate unit, Ole Krarup Leth, at +45 23 82 72 23 or by e-mail at okl@dmi.dk or senior scientist and IcyAlert project leader Tian Tian at+45 24 81 32 03 or by e-mail tian@dmi.dk .




Apply now 

Please enclose a cover letter, a curriculum vitae (incl. publication list) and contacts for relevant professional references. Please note that applications may be shared with relevant project partners from DTU and RMI as a part of the recruitment process.

At DMI, diversity is an important value to us because we believe that an inclusive, versatile work environment strengthens task fulfilment. We actively work to foster diversity in our employee composition, reflected in our inclusive workplace and a balance between work and family life. We encourage everyone to apply for the position regardless of age, gender, sexuality, religion or ethnicity.




To apply for the position, please use the official link and follow the instructions.

Title: One or more PhD Positions in Unsupervised Learning for Medical Image Analysis
Description:
At the Faculty of Medicine, Department of Health Science and Technology, one or more PhD stipends in Unsupervised Learning for Medical Image Analysis are available for appointment from November 1, 2026, or as soon as possible thereafter.



The appointment is for a period of three years.



The successful candidate will be enrolled in the PhD programme in Biomedical Engineering and Neuroscience at the Faculty of Medicine.



Who we are



The Department of Health Science and Technology (HST) at Aalborg University is an interdisciplinary research and teaching environment where engineering, medicine and health sciences come together to improve people's lives. 



As a PhD fellow at HST, you will become part of an international research community with access to experienced supervisors, modern research facilities and strong interdisciplinary collaboration. You will work alongside researchers from a wide range of disciplines and engage with hospitals, industry and public-sector partners to address some of society's most important health challenges.



The department is home to approximately 180 academic staff members, around 100 PhD fellows and more than 1,700 students. We offer a stimulating research environment that encourages scientific curiosity, collaboration and professional development.



The Faculty of Medicine is committed to preparing PhD graduates for diverse career paths. Throughout your PhD, you will develop advanced research competencies alongside transferable skills that prepare you for careers in academia, industry and the public sector. Towards the end of your PhD, you will be offered dedicated career development support to help you plan your next career step.



At HST, our values – Share. Care. Dare. – shape the way we collaborate, support one another and create knowledge with societal impact.



Learn more about the department on our website and in our research portal.



Opportunistic screening envisions a scenario in which all acquired medical images are studied in minute detail to detect the early signs of any disease. When combined with AI tools, this has the potential to

detect diseases earlier, giving the best chance of improving patient outcomes
reduce the burden placed on radiologists and democratize diagnostic expertise to more healthcare institutions
maximize the utility of collected radiological data

One of the major barriers to achieving this, is figuring out how to learn useful patterns in the data without relying on exhaustive labelling. For example, in the anomaly detection setting, we often assume that only healthy images are available during training. Using this, we wish to learn the appearance and structure of healthy anatomy and detect any deviation from the healthy distribution. But in the absence of labels, how should we direct the model to learn relevant features, and how can we determine which features are relevant? These questions are at the core of anomaly detection and despite being a well-established field of research, these are still very much open problems.



To this end, we are looking for candidates interested in developing new machine learning methods for medical image analysis, with a particular focus in anomaly detection and unsupervised learning. In this position, you will have the chance to explore basic machine learning research as well as more applied projects. While most of the work will involve technical machine learning research, you will also have access to clinical experts and will be expected to collaborate closely with other researchers in the Faculty of Medicine and at Aalborg University Hospital.



Applicants should have:

A strong technical background in machine learning, computing, data science, biomedical engineering, or a related field at the level of a master degree
Programming skills (Python) and experience with common machine learning platforms
Experience with deep learning, computer vision, medical image analysis or unsupervised learning is an advantage.
English language skills, both written and spoken

Qualification requirements



PhD stipends are allocated to individuals who hold a Master's degree. PhD stipends are normally for a period of 3 years. It is a prerequisite for allocation of the stipend that the candidate will be enrolled as a PhD student at the Doctoral School in Medicine, Biomedical Science and Technologyin accordance with the regulations of Ministerial Order No. 1124 of September 19, 2025 on the PhD Programme at the Universities and Certain Higher Artistic Educational Institutions. According to the Ministerial Order, the progress of the PhD student shall be assessed at regular points in time. As part of the PhD study, you are among other things required to complete PhD courses corresponding to 30 ECTS, gain experience with teaching or other forms of knowledge dissemination and complete an external research stay outside of Aalborg University, preferably 3-6 months at a foreign research institution.



How to apply



Your application must include the following:

Application, stating reasons for applying and qualifications in relation to the position
Curriculum Vitae (CV)
Diplomas (bachelor's and master's degree diploma, including grades) 
Research statement (max 1 page excluding references), briefly describing a proposed research project. Include a problem description, a brief summary of existing solutions, and your proposed approach/topic that you would like to investigate.
References (optional)
Other relevant documents

The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website. 



Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position.

Shortlisting will be applied. This means that after the application deadline, the head of the department, with the assistance of the hiring committee, will select the applicants to be assessed. All applicants will be informed whether they have been shortlisted for assessment or not.



The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace.

The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Job Description

We are looking for a Data Solutions Developer to join our growing SmartPropulsion team in Aalborg. You will develop data models, APIs, analytical solutions, and internal tools supporting the optimization of propulsion systems for large sea-going vessels.

You will contribute to Emerson Smart-Propulsion and Aperio Insight, our cloud-based business intelligence platform, transforming vessel data into scalable solutions and valuable customer insights.




In This Role, Your Responsibilities Will Be:




Develop and maintain PostgreSQL data models supporting marine applications and analytical products.
Design, build, and maintain APIs for vessel data, models, and related services.
Create and maintain digital vessel models using onboard and third-party data.
Develop data products, including predictive maintenance models, KPIs, and operational insights.
Build visualizations and internal tools using Streamlit or similar technologies.
Collaborate with Customer Success, Sales, and development colleagues in a sprint-based environment.




Who You Are:




You enjoy turning complex data into practical and scalable solutions. You are collaborative, technically curious, and comfortable working in a small, growing team where priorities may evolve.

You take ownership of your work, manage complexity effectively, and communicate technical information clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

A bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Science, Engineering, or a related field.
At least three years of relevant experience in software development, data engineering, or data science.
Advanced experience with Python, PostgreSQL, and relational data modelling.
Experience developing APIs and deploying data visualizations or internal applications.
Experience with data science tools such as PyTorch, CUDA, or scikit-learn.
Professional proficiency in English and experience developing in Linux environments.




Preferred Qualifications That Set You Apart:




Knowledge of Kubernetes, containers, and cloud-based data platforms.
Experience with Rust or another systems programming language.
Experience working with operational, industrial, or time-series data.
Knowledge of predictive maintenance, performance optimization, or condition monitoring.
Familiarity with maritime systems, vessels, or industrial applications.
Experience using AI-assisted development tools for coding, testing, and verification.

Description:
About TetraScience

TetraScience is the Scientific Data and AI Company building Tetra OS, the operating system for scientific intelligence. We help the world's leading life sciences firms turn fragmented scientific data into AI-native assets and scientific workflows that accelerate discovery, development, and manufacturing. TetraScience's growing ecosystem of strategic partners includes NVIDIA, Databricks, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Snowflake, Google, and Microsoft.

In connection with your candidacy, you will be asked to carefully review "The Tetra Way," authored by our CEO, Patrick Grady; it is impossible to overstate the importance of this document, and you should take it literally as you decide whether our mission, culture, and expectations are right for you.


Who You Are

You are a product-minded, outcome-obsessed driver of technical scientific solutions.

You a high velocity self-starter. You refuse to let uncertainty obstruct your path to designing and building solutions.

You roll up your sleeves, try things out, and get things done. You do not hesitate to prototype, demo, and build in order to accelerate delivery of products for your end users.

You thrive in environments where you can collaborate with scientists, product managers, and engineers to transform complex scientific data into actionable outcomes. Your ability to engage with scientists and business leaders alike makes you a key player in maximizing the value of scientific data.

With rich experience applying cutting edge data methodologies to the biopharma R&D domain, you bridge understanding between present-day pain points and generalizable solutions.

You are an insatiable learner, with a track record of deeply learning new tools, methods, and domains.

You fundamentally embody the principles of extreme ownership and have a demonstrated history of building extensible data models and applications for Biopharma end users to maximize value from their data via analysis and integration with AI/ML.

This role will require extreme self-discipline and determination as we forge a category that will fundamentally and forever change the life science industry.


What You Have Done


PhD with +4 years or Masters with +8 years of industry experience in life sciences  with extensive domain knowledge in drug discovery (target ID through lead optimization), preclinical development, CMC (all drug modalities), or product quality testing
Proven track record of defining, designing, prototyping, and implementing productized AI/ML-driven use cases in cloud environments
Collaborated with cross-functional teams, including product managers, software engineers, and scientific stakeholders
Performed extensive exploratory data analysis and workflow optimization to enable scientific outcomes not previously possible
Engaged diverse audiences, from scientists to executive stakeholders using your excellent communication and storytelling abilities
Advised scientists in a consulting capacity to further research, development, and quality testing outcomes


Requirements

What You Will Do



You will be a critical team member in a unique partnership to industrialize Scientific AI. As such, you will engage directly with customers onsite and will need to travel up to 25% of your time, building strong relationships, deeply understanding their scientific data challenges and requirements, and accelerating solutions
Design and implement extensible, reusable data models that efficiently capture and organize scientific data for scientific use cases, ensuring scalability and future adaptability
Translate scientific data workflows into robust solutions leveraging the Tetra Data Platform
Own, scope, prototype, and implement solutions including:
Data model design (tabular & JSON)
Python-based parser development
Lab software (e.g., ELN/LIMS) integration via APIs
Data visualization and app development in Python (using app frameworks like Streamlit and plotting tools like holoviews and Plotly) 
Collaborate with Scientific Business Analysts (SBAs), customer scientists and applied AI engineers to develop and deploy models (ML, AI, mechanistic, statistical, hybrid)
Programmatically interrogating proprietary instrument output files
Dynamically iterate with scientific end users and technical stakeholders to rapidly drive solution development and adoption through regular demos and meetings
Proactively communicate implementation progress and deliver demos to customer stakeholders
Collaborate with the product team to build and prioritize our roadmap by understanding customers' pain points within and outside Tetra Data Platform
Rapidly learn new technologies (e.g., new AWS services or scientific analysis applications) to develop and troubleshoot use cases


Benefits



Competitive Salary and equity in a fast-growing company
Supportive, team-oriented culture of continuous improvement
Generous paid time off (PTO)
Flexible working arrangements - Remote work when not at Customer Sites

Working end-to-end to solve problems with a product and customer-oriented mindset.

Involvement in developing statistical models.
Collaborating with the rest of the team to improve our product and solve customer problems.

Has established experience within a similar role.
Experience using Python and deploying to production.
First-hand experience with ML libraries, frameworks, and tools, such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, Scikit-learn, Prophet, DeepAR, etc.
Degree educated within a technical field (Computer Science or equivalent engineering degree).
Experience in a cloud environment (AWS, Google Cloud, or Azure).
Bonus: experience with dbt, Snowflake, Airflow, or Metaflow; experience in complex ML system design; and experience in statistical hypothesis testing.

Develop and maintain the backbone of our personalization engine, which is used by millions of users every day to support their efforts to combat food waste.

To be part of an international company, with over 1,300+ colleagues across 20 countries.


Our values


We win together: Food waste is a big beast to fight. We can do it if we win together as Waste Warriors with no ego. We believe in a #oneteam.
We raise the bar: We always push for more. We work smart, smash barriers, and elevate one another.
We keep it simple: Our ambitions are bold but our solutions are simple.

We care: We always look out for each other. Caring is also about the way we do business. We do the right thing.

Please also check our website and international media in order to get a good overview of Too Good To Go.
Please submit your CV and Cover letter in English.

Title: Postdoc in Probabilistic Methods for Sequential Decision-Making - DTU Compute
Place: Kongens Lyngby, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
Description:
Job Description

Are you interested in probabilistic machine learning, uncertainty quantification, and sequential decision-making?

Then this post-doc position may be for you.

DTU Compute invites applications for a fully funded post-doc position with a duration up to two years.

The position is part of the research grant “Active Inference for Dynamic Pricing”, funded by the Fund of 20th December. The overall aim of the project is to investigate active inference as a principled framework for developing robust methods for sequential decision-making under uncertainty, building on state-of-the-art machine learning methods and architectures. The project will investigate and validate the developed methodology through several real-world applications, including dynamic pricing.

You will be part of the Section for Cognitive Systems , a dynamic and research-oriented group of scientists, technical personnel, and administrative staff. We have a broad interest in machine learning and information processing in humans and computers and a particular focus on the signals they exchange.

Responsibilities

As a postdoctoral researcher, you will conduct independent and collaborative research on probabilistic machine learning and active inference for sequential decision-making under uncertainty. Your work will involve developing novel models and algorithms, as well as implementing and evaluating them using modern machine learning frameworks. You will investigate the proposed methodology through realistic use cases, including dynamic pricing. The position also includes disseminating research results through publications in leading international journals and conferences, and participating in scientific collaborations. As a post-doc, you will also contribute to the academic environment at DTU Compute, including limited teaching and supervision activities.

Qualifications:


Proven expert knowledge and experience in probabilistic machine learning and deep learning
Excellent analytical and mathematical problem-solving skills
Excellent programming skills (Python and modern machine learning frameworks like PyTorch, JaX, etc.) and experience in working with HPC/GPU environments
A track record of publication and presentation of research results in quality journals/conferences.


As a formal qualification, you must hold a PhD degree (or equivalent) in machine learning, signal processing, data science or a related field.

We offer

DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and terms of employment

The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. In addition, supplements can be negotiated in accordance with DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures .

The period of employment is two years with a starting date as soon as possible subject to mutual agreement. The position is a full-time position.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here .

Further information

For further information, contact Associate Professor Bjørn Sand Jensen ( bjje@dtu.dk ) or Associate Professor Michael Riis Andersen ( miri@dtu.dk ) from the section of Cognitive Systems at DTU Compute.

You can read more about the DTU Compute at www.compute.dtu.dk/ and the section at www.compute.dtu.dk/sections/cogsys .

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark .

Application procedure

Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 22 October 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:


Application (cover letter)
CV
Academic Diplomas (MSc/PhD – in English)
Full list of publications. Highlight 1-5 key publications, briefly explain your contribution and argue the significance of each (max 100 words per publication)
Research statement, including how your background fits the position (max 2 pages)


Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Compute

DTU Compute – Department of Applied Mathematics and Computer Science – is an internationally recognised academic environment with over 400 employees and 10 research sections. We broadly cover digital technologies within mathematics, data science, computer science, and computer engineering, including artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, internet of things (IoT), chip design, cybersecurity, human-computer interaction, social networks, fairness, and data ethics. Our research is rooted in basic research and centres on mathematical models of the physical and virtual world, as a basis for the analysis, design, and implementation of complex systems. We focus on ensuring that our research results contribute to creating a better society by supporting areas such as health, green transition, energy supply, and life science. We collaborate with universities, public and private organisations, and companies in Denmark and abroad, and through DTU’s startup ecosystem, we encourage innovation and entrepreneurship. We have a strong ethical, human, and sustainable approach that ensures integrity in our work. Therefore, we strive for and take responsibility for driving the democratisation of digital technologies, so that everyone has the opportunity to actively participate in the development, and we ensure a continued open, democratic, and inclusive society for the benefit of all. At DTU Compute, we value diversity, inclusion, and a flexible work-life balance.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829

DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

Title: Working in power markets? Let's talk
Place: Copenhagen Municipality, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
Description:
Electricity Maps is building the world's most comprehensive electricity data platform. Real-time, historical, and forecasted electricity mix, prices, load, and carbon intensity across markets worldwide.

Power markets are a wide, fast-moving space and one with a lot of room for someone with the right experience to help shape what direction we take. That's why we'd rather meet you now even if we don't have an official role on the page. From there, we can figure out together what makes sense. We especially love hearing from people who come with a view: where you'd add value, what you'd want to work on or what you think we're missing.

Maybe you work in one of the following areas:


Day-ahead and intraday forecasting
BESS and asset optimization
Imbalance and balancing markets
Renewable generation forecasting (wind, solar, etc.)
Power market analytics or trading
Something adjacent


We're interested in talking across all lines of work in these areas: Engineering, ML, product, commercial, analytics, or something else. Whatever angle you come at it from, we're curious to hear it.

What to expect

We read every intro that comes through. If we see something we want to learn more about, we'll reach out to get to know each other and figure out together where your experience could add the most value.

About Electricity Maps

There are two sides to what we do. The first: decarbonizing the grid by making historical, real-time, and forecasted data on electricity mix, load, and carbon intensity available to anyone making smarter decisions across the energy transition.

The second is newer for us - we've started working with energy traders, asset operators, and BESS players in European power markets, building out price forecasting, market signals, and adjacent tooling. It's an area we're growing fast in and one with plenty of room for the right person to help shape where it goes.

The details


Location: Copenhagen (in-office with flexibility)
Compensation: Competitive salary + stock options (when a role materializes)
Benefits: 6 weeks vacation, health insurance, annual company offsite, lunch and snacks at office

Title: Senior Analyst - Consumer Credit Risk & Underwriting
Place: Copenhagen, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
Description:
Klarna, briefly

At Klarna, we're building an everyday finance network, helping over 120 million consumers across 26 countries save time and money, and worry less about their finances.Working at Klarna means taking on problems most companies never get to solve, and being hands-on enough that the interesting part of the work lands with you, not someone else. You'll build with AI, not watch it happen.

This is the stretch zone. Come find out what you're capable of.

About The Role

Klarna is bringing its Fair Financing product live in Denmark. As a Senior Analyst on the credit decisioning team, you'll build and defend the underwriting policies that decide who gets credit in Denmark and on what terms, working from bureau data and models built specifically for the Danish market.

You'll work alongside Product, Risk, and the regional Belgium team to bring that policy onto Klarna's Global Underwriting Platform (GUP), the shared framework that will power credit decisions across markets.

What You'll Do


You'll analyze consumer credit risk using SQL and Danish credit bureau data to find where underwriting policy should tighten or loosen.
You'll work with Product, Risk, and the Danish regional team to bring Denmark’s credit policy onto Klarna's Global Underwriting Platform.
You'll align purchase power and pre-qualification logic for the Danish market across Klarna's App and its One Card product.
You'll monitor how the Danish bureau data feeding your models performs, and flag where sourcing or model quality needs to change.
You'll turn what your analysis shows into policy changes that underwriting, product, and the regional team can act on directly.


Who you are


You've worked in consumer credit risk, underwriting, or credit policy, and you understand how a policy change affects both approval rates and portfolio health.
You're proficient in SQL and comfortable working directly with large, messy datasets.
You know credit bureau data, repayment behavior, and credit risk modeling well enough to spot where the numbers don't add up.
You work through ambiguous or inconsistent policy logic methodically until you find the actual root cause.
You can turn a data finding into a policy change that underwriting, product, and regional teams can each act on.


Bonus points for


A degree in Finance, Economics, Data Science, Mathematics, or a related quantitative field.


Things you should know before applying


Working together: we value co-located teams; most teams currently meet in the office 2–3 days per week, and this varies by team and can change over time.
Non-obvious backgrounds are welcome. Diversity of skills, perspectives and backgrounds is how we create, innovate, and disrupt like no other.
Final compensation will be based on the candidate's qualifications, skills, and experience.
Depending on your background, this could land as an Analyst role or a Data Scientist role — we'll settle the exact title with you once we understand your experience.


Please include a CV in English.

Curious to learn more about Klarna and what it’s like to work here? Explore our career site.

Title: PHD Graduate Student
Description:
Postdoctoral Researcher in Biodiversity Forecasting, Vegetation Dynamics and Rewilding

Department of Biology — Section for Ecoinformatics and Biodiversity, Aarhus University

Are you interested in building spatially explicit forecasts of how rural depopulation, climate and land-use change, and alternative rewilding pathways could reshape plant diversity and ecosystem functioning across Europe? The Department of Biology at Aarhus University is inviting applications for a two-year postdoctoral position, offering a great opportunity to join the new Biodiversa+ REDESIGN project.

Start date: 1 January 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter

Duration: Fixed-term, full-time, 1 January 2027 – 31 December 2029

Location: Ny Munkegade 114, 8000 Aarhus C, Denmark (some travel for project meetings expected)

About the role

The postdoctoral researcher will model how depopulation and rewilding affect biodiversity and ecosystem structure under rising biosphere novelty, integrating ecological, demographic, environmental, and remote-sensing data into scenario-based forecasts of European vegetation and biodiversity dynamics. The position is embedded within ECONOVO, a research center focused on providing the scientific foundation to steer emerging environmental conditions toward outcomes that sustain global biodiversity.

Main responsibilities:

Assemble, harmonize, and analyze large spatial and temporal biodiversity datasets (vegetation-plot, environmental, land-use, demographic, and remote-sensing data)
Develop spatially explicit forecasts of plant diversity and community change under alternative climate, socioeconomic, land-use, depopulation, and rewilding scenarios, with projections extending to 2100 (and, where appropriate, 2300)

Strong practical expertise in SAS programming, including the ability to produce high-quality, well-documented analysis outputs; familiarity with R will be an added value
Experience with CDISC standards, including ADaM and SDTM, and familiarity with relevant regulatory guidelines is an advantage; alternatively, a strong motivation to learn and apply these standards
Interest in applied statistics and statistical analysis of clinical or healthcare data, with willingness to develop further in clinical trial analyses, meta-analyses, or indirect treatment comparison methods

In this role, your main interfaces will be with fellow statistical programmers and biostatisticians, with occasional collaboration across Medical Affairs, HEOR, and Market Access.

Assistant Professor for Computational Non-Target Screening of Contaminants of Emerging Concern

The Analytical Chemistry Group invites applications for a 4-year assistant professorship in machine learning–based non-target screening of contaminants, CECs and other complex chemical mixtures.

The position is within analytical chemistry with a focus on machine learning–based non-target screening of contaminants of emerging concern (CECs) and related chemical fingerprints in complex environmental and biological matrices. The research combines high-resolution mass spectrometry, complementary chromatographic separations (LC, online-SPE-LC, SFC and GC×GC), and analytical data science to develop scalable workflows for targeted, suspect and non-target screening. The aim is to transform large HRMS datasets from drinking water, wastewater, sludge, advanced treatment systems and human urine into chemical annotations, exposure signatures and understanding of contaminant fate, removal and human exposure.

The position will contribute to two closely connected research directions: identification of micropollutants, including highly polar, persistent, mobile and fluorinated compounds, in wastewater, sludge and advanced treatment systems to support machine-learning models for contaminant fate and removal; and large-scale profiling of the human urinary exposome to identify chemical exposure signatures associated with disease.

The research is based on complementary chromatography-HRMS workflows, including LC, online-SPE-LC, SFC and GC×GC coupled to Orbitrap, QqTOF and TOF platforms. A central task is to develop reproducible and scalable data workflows that integrate automatic preprocessing, cheminformatics, chemical databases and machine learning for compound identification, annotation, prioritization, confidence annotation, and quantitative or semi-quantitative interpretation.

The position has a strong analytical data science profile. We are particularly interested in candidates who can develop and critically validate open, transparent and reusable workflows for large HRMS datasets, including programming-based data processing, AI-assisted code development, workflow benchmarking, molecular pattern recognition, and integration of experimental analytical chemistry with predictive modelling.

We seek ambitious candidates with a strong profile in analytical chemistry, separation science, HRMS and/or analytical data science, and with motivation to work in close collaboration with academic, clinical, regulatory and industrial partners.

Who are we looking for?

Ideal Applicants Should Have


A PhD in analytical chemistry, environmental chemistry, bioanalytical chemistry, metabolomics, exposomics, chemometrics, computational chemistry, analytical data science or a closely related discipline
Documented experience with HRMS-based targeted, suspect and/or non-target screening workflows for complex environmental or biological samples
Experience with large-scale analytical datasets, including feature detection, alignment, blank filtering, annotation, prioritization, benchmarking and quality control
Experience with cheminformatics, including the use of chemical databases, spectral libraries, molecular fingerprints, in-silico prediction tools and computational approaches for compound annotation.
Programming skills, for example in Python, R or MATLAB, for processing and interpretation of chromatography and mass spectral data. Experience with reproducible code, AI-assisted coding, prompt engineering, code validation and debugging is an advantage
Experience with complementary chromatographic approaches such as LC, online-SPE-LC, SFC, GC or multidimensional chromatography is an advantage
Experience with CEC analysis, highly polar or mobile contaminants, PFAS or organofluorine screening, wastewater, sludge, urine, exposomics and/or machine learning-based modelling is highly advantageous
Documented experience with scientific writing, including peer-reviewed publications and grant or fellowship applications
Proven ability to lead research activities independently, contribute strategically to interdisciplinary projects and collaborate constructively within a research group


The assistant professor’s duties are research and teaching, including obligations with regard to publication/scientific communication, within Computational Non-Target Screening of Contaminants of Emerging Concern. To a limited extent this may also include performance of other duties.

Assessment of applicants will primarily consider their level of documented, internationally competitive research. The ability to attract external funding will be considered together with outreach qualifications. Teaching qualifications are not mandatory, but an interest in teaching is essential and documented teaching qualifications and teaching experience will be considered an advantage.

General criteria apply to the appointment of Assistant Professors at the University of Copenhagen. The criteria (research, teaching, Innovation & societal impact, organizational contribution and leadership) are considered as a framework for an overall assessment of the applicant. In addition, each applicant will be assessed according to the specific requirements listed in this advertisement.

Title: Specialist, Machine Learning Engineer
Place: Copenhagen, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
Description:
Specialist | Full-Time

Digital Solutions & Development > Digital Solutions > AI/ML Chapter

Do you enjoy creating and scaling AI/ML solutions that deliver meaningful business results? Do you have experience in designing, developing and deploying AI/ML solutions and want to advance your career? Do you enjoy working at the intersection of product, engineering and business to turn advanced AI capabilities into production-ready solutions? Then you might be our new AI/ML Engineer. We are hiring across multiple seniority levels, and the role will be aligned to your experience, technical skills, and demonstrated impact.

At the core of Digital Development Platform organization, AI/ML Chapter serves as the capability home for AI/ML specialization, supporting engineering excellence, skills development, and scalable delivery across Vestas. You will be part of a global team spanning Denmark and India, partnering closely with product owners, AI/ML engineers and business stakeholders to design, build, and scale AI/ML, GenAI, and agentic solutions across Vestas value chain.

As part of the broader Autonomous Flows area, the team contributes to building next-generation intelligent systems and agentic workflows that enhance operational efficiency and unlock new business value. We collaborate closely with platform, product and governance teams to ensure scalable, responsible, and impactful adoption of AI across Vestas. With disciplined engineering practices, data-focused methods, and close collaboration with business partners, the team continually raises AI/ML delivery standards and enables meaningful solutions that improve visibility, optimization, and innovation across the enterprise.

Responsibilities

In this role, you will collaborate with product owners, ML engineers, application developers and business SMEs to build and scale advanced ML/GenAI and agent-based systems embedded in digital products. This role emphasizes reasoning-driven AI, self-directed execution and significant informal leadership to deliver results across the organization.


Contribute to validating and conducting technical feasibility assessments of high-impact ML/GenAI use cases
Build, productize and scale ML/GenAI and agentic systems capable of reasoning, planning and carrying out complex tasks
Integrate AI/ML capabilities into enterprise applications, enabling seamless, human-in-the-loop and self-directed decision-making
Work with cross-functional product teams in delivering AI/ML initiatives while advising stakeholders on responsible AI adoption balancing experimentation with production considerations such as performance, cost, reliability and governance
Establish and promote reusable patterns and engineering standards for scalable delivery, AI-ready data, and trusted AI automation


Qualifications

You have a solid foundation in machine learning and software engineering, combined with clear communication and stakeholder engagement skills. You bring extensive experience in designing and scaling production-grade AI/ML systems, with experience leading solutions across the full lifecycle from problem framing to deployment and continuous improvement. 


A master's degree in a relevant field (e.g., computer science, data science, engineering) or equivalent practical experience
You have demonstrated depth in one of the fields such as NLP, generative AI, agentic systems, computer vision, ML engineering or large-scale AI systems
5+ years of experience in ML engineering, including design, delivery and scaling of production-grade AI/ML solutions; the role can be aligned to different seniority levels based on skill level and demonstrated impact
Deep knowledge of Python, ability to develop production grade code, solid experience with ML frameworks (e.g., Scikit-learn, Tensorflow, Pytorch) and GenAI/Agentic frameworks (e.g., Langchain, LangGraph, Pydantic AI)
Deep experience with AI experimentation and modeling, as well as designing robust, scalable training and inference pipelines on cloud platforms including Azure and Snowflake, deployed through CI/CD within an IaC environment
Solid experience with RESTful API design, Docker-based containerization, and Kubernetes-based deployment, scaling, and operations


Competencies


Productionize ML, LLM/GenAI models and agentic systems into reliable, high-performance services with optimized latency, throughput and cost efficiency
Design and operate scalable batch and real-time ML pipelines with high reproducibility across training and deployment
Establish robust monitoring and observability for model performance, data quality, system health and data drift detection
Manage the full ML lifecycle with clear versioning, governance, automated retraining and resilient deployment strategies
Effectively leverage AI-assisted development tools (e.g., GitHub Copilot, Claude Code) to accelerate prototyping, improve engineering quality and enhance developer productivity in building AI/ML and GenAI solutions


 Global Collaboration & Enablement


Effective collaboration across geographically distributed teams (Denmark, India, Portugal), with high cross-cultural awareness and communication
Ability to align product, AI/ML engineering, platform and MLOps teams to deliver shared engineering outcomes
Demonstrated experience in mentoring and enabling teams through knowledge sharing, best practices and informal leadership


What We Offer

Purpose. An opportunity to help address climate change and support future generations through building AI/ML, GenAI and agentic solutions that power the future of renewable energy and sustainable operations.

Accelerated learning and growth. Join a high-caliber global team of AI/ML engineers, data scientists and GenAI practitioners, with clear focus on continuous learning, knowledge sharing and expanding into agentic autonomous flows.

Global collaboration & collaborative team culture. Work within a multicultural Denmark-India setup that values trust, collaboration and mutual support to deliver meaningful impact.

Opportunity to shape your role. Play a key role in scaling agentic autonomous flows and high-value AI/ML solutions, with the freedom to shape direction, approaches, and outcomes.

Supportive and inclusive environment. Thrive in a diverse, inclusive workplace that promotes well-being, work-life balance and enables individuals to bring their full potential to work.

Career growth in a global organization. Join a global organization that supports ongoing skill development and career advancement

Overall, we offer you the opportunity to contribute meaningfully while growing your career in a global, multicultural environment that promotes continuous learning and development.

It has come to our attention that there are a number of fraudulent emails from people pretending to work for Vestas. Read more via this link, www.vestas.com/en/careers/job-openings.

At Vestas, we recognize the value of diversity, equity, and inclusion in driving innovation and success. We strongly encourage individuals from all backgrounds to apply, particularly those who may hesitate due to their identity or feel they do not meet every criterion. As our CEO states, "Expertise and talent come in many forms, and a diverse workforce enhances our ability to think differently and solve the complex challenges of our industry". Your unique perspective is what will help us powering the solution for a sustainable, green energy future.

About Vestas

Vestas is the energy industry’s global partner on sustainable energy solutions. We are specialised in designing, manufacturing, installing, and servicing wind turbines, both onshore and offshore. Across the globe, we have installed more wind power than anyone else. We consider ourselves pioneers within the industry, as we continuously aim to design new solutions and technologies to create a more sustainable future for all of us. With more than 173 GW of wind power installed worldwide and 40+ years of experience in wind energy, we have an unmatched track record demonstrating our expertise within the field. With 29,000 employees globally, we are a diverse team united by a common goal: to power the solution – today, tomorrow, and far into the future. Vestas promotes a diverse workforce which embraces all social identities and is free of any discrimination. We commit to create and sustain an environment that acknowledges and harvests different experiences, skills, and perspectives. We also aim to give everyone equal access to opportunity. To learn more about our company and life at Vestas, we invite you to visit our website at www.vestas.com and follow us on our social media channels. Title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer
Place: Copenhagen, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
Description:
Veo is an AI-powered sports camera and analysis ecosystem built for one job: turning what happens on a pitch into proof. Capture, viewing, data and analytics, sharing- all in one system, all pointed at the same thing.

That's bigger than football. Every player, on every pitch, gets access to the kind of proof only the top academies used to keep for themselves. It's the future we're building.

Every youth match still has a moment nobody saw. A run that won the game, underneath everyone's radar. A kid written off before anyone actually checked. We exist to close that gap, one match at a time.

One camera on any pitch feeds an AI that tracks every player and the ball for the whole game, turning what happened into evidence instead of somebody's opinion.

That's the actual job here. Not shipping features. Building the system that gives proof to someone who used to rely on a hunch.

If you've ever watched a match and wondered who else saw what you saw, you already know why this matters.

We're looking for people who want to build that future with us.

The Opportunity

As a Senior Machine Learning Engineer at Veo you will get to work on challenging problems and directly contribute to the value created by our AI-driven end-user products.

You will become part of our AI team, which comprises 20+ researchers and engineers responsible for all stages in the machine learning lifecycles across different projects - from scoping and defining data annotation tasks to modeling, validation, and deployment. You will take ownership of the direction and execution of your projects while collaborating closely with the rest of the team, exchanging feedback, and helping others improve and succeed.

We stay current with the latest research and continuously discuss concepts and ideas in recent papers to assess their relevance to our tasks and product-specific challenges.

We are looking for an ambitious, high-performing senior engineer or researcher with a strong track record of delivering real-world machine learning systems. You should bring the technical depth and judgment needed to make sound decisions in complex and sometimes ambiguous environments.

What you will do:



Train state-of-the-art machine learning models
Write efficient inference pipelines for cloud and edge
Define and supervise data annotation tasks
Improve evaluation schemes to increase understanding of model performance and shortcomings
Contribute to long-term planning and prioritization of tasks
Mentor colleagues and raise the technical bar through feedback, knowledge sharing, and collaboration




What you could bring:



MSc or PhD in a relevant field, or equivalent practical experience
Extensive hands-on experience delivering real-world, large-scale machine learning projects
Strong coding and software engineering skills, with experience building maintainable production systems
Experience taking ownership of technically complex projects from concept to deployment
Sound technical judgment and the ability to navigate ambiguity and balance research, product, and engineering considerations
A rigorous and critical approach to examining details, assumptions, and results
Strong communication skills and the ability to influence technical direction across teams




Our Copenhagen office mirrors our innovative technology – with an indoor ball court, rooftop terrace, and well-equipped gym. We have created a facility that supports connecting disciplines across the business, facilitates creative thinking, and gives the space to engage with colleagues, our global partners, and the entire Veo community.

Values we hold at Veo:

Dare - We take initiative, stay curious, and challenge the status quo in our work.

Own it - We drive impact by identifying opportunities, taking responsibility, and confidently executing.

Level up - We embrace growth, continuously learning and shaping our skills.

Play as a team - We collaborate across a diverse organization, leveraging shared insights for stronger

outcomes.

Customer Centric - We deliver value by having close partnerships and a deep understanding of our customers (internally and externally)

We value diversity and inclusion and welcome applicants from all backgrounds, even if your experience doesn’t completely match every qualification listed. What matters most is your creativity, potential, and ability to make meaningful contributions.

Title: Uopfordret ansøgning til Software Engineering, Tech. Management & Data Intelligence
Place: Copenhagen Municipality, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
Description:
Stillingsbeskrivelse

Sopra Steria er en IT-konsulentforretning med fokus på softwareudvikling, projektledelse og data/analyse. Vi hjælper i dag særligt finansielle institutioner og den offentlige sektor med at nå deres ambitioner. Vi kombinerer moderne teknologi og en solid forretningsforståelse for at sikre, at vi finder løsninger, som både er attraktive, værdiskabende og er teknisk mulige at gennemføre samt implementere. Vi er med fra start til slut.

Siden 2015 har vi været i top-10 som ”Danmarks bedste it-virksomhed” i ”Great Place To Works” årlige undersøgelse, og vi er i høj grad drevet af at skabe et godt, socialt og uformelt arbejdsmiljø med fokus på resultater og det gode arbejdsliv i balance. Det er fundamentalt for os, at vores medarbejdere har det godt, og syntes at det er sjovt at gå på arbejde, det er sådan vi skaber de bedste resultater.

Lyder det interessant så bliv en del af vores talent pipeline (søg uopfordret), da vi igennem året løbende søger konsulenter indenfor vores tre kompetenceområder...

Technology management


Projektleder, produktleder, business analyst, enterprise arkitekt og forretningskonsulent.


Data Intelligence


Data engineer, data analyst, automation specialist, RPA specialist, AI/ML Engineer og data scientist.


Software udvikling


.Net og Java udviklere


Vi tilbyder:


Lækre kontorlokaler i hjertet af København.
Søde og dedikerede kollegaer, som glæder sig til at arbejde sammen med dig.
En uformel og sjov hverdag på en spændende arbejdsplads med en hyggelig omgangstone
Gode muligheder med fokus på både personlig og faglig udvikling.
Regelmæssige sociale arrangementer som fredagsbar, onsdagstræning, sommerfest etc.
Fleksibel arbejdsplads med mulighed for både at arbejde fra vores kontor, hos kunden eller hjemmefra.


Bliv en del af en arbejdsplads hvor der er god mulighed personlig og faglig udvikling. Vi vækster hele tiden, hvilket giver gode muligheder for at få mere ansvar i takt med at virksomheden vokser.

Interesseret i at blive en del af Sopra Steria?

Send din ansøgning og dit CV, så kontakter vi dig, hvis vi ser, at vi har muligheder, der passer til dig. Vi ser frem til at modtage din ansøgning.

OBS! Ansøgninger besvares kun i så fald vi åbner en matchende rolle til din profil. Undersøg derfor gerne nuværende åbninger før du søger.

Yderligere oplysninger

Vi er en af nordens førende konsulentvirksomheder inden for digitalisering, innovation og moderne teknologi og gennem mange år har vi været rangeret som en af Danmarks bedste IT-arbejdspladser.

Som en af nordens største konsulentvirksomheder bistår vi store private virksomheder og offentlige organisationer med deres digitale omstilling.

Vi lægger vægt på at skabe værdi for vores kunder og samfundet og har som mål at skabe en bedre og mere bæredygtig fremtid.
