Title: Data Scientist
Description:
Who We Are

Optima Partners is an advanced data and business consultancy headquartered in Edinburgh, UK. We are a practitioner-led organisation that collaborates with top consumer brands to drive transformation and foster customer-centricity through our expertise in customer strategy, innovative design, and advanced data science and engineering.

We work with leading consumer brands to tackle and overcome complex business and customer problems, drive transformation and champion customer-centric agendas. We are proud to include leading UK and global brands among our current clients, including Lloyds Banking Group, NatWest Group, Bank of Ireland, Nationwide, Aviva, Biogen, Eon Next, OVO, Virgin Media O2, BT, HMD Global, Centrica and GSK. We are obsessive about delivering value for our clients and work in a collaborative, engaged and creative way with our colleagues and clients. We strive to support the transition of knowledge and capability into strategic teams.

The opportunity

We are looking for an Associate Consultant - Data Science to support the application of machine learning, statistical modelling and experimentation to solve complex business problems and drive measurable outcomes across our client base. Working hands-on with data, you will help develop analytical approaches, build and validate models, run tests and translate data into clear, actionable insights.

This is an exciting opportunity for an enthusiastic data science professional with up to one year of commercial experience, or equivalent project experience, to develop consulting and technical skills across a variety of commercial sectors. At Optima, you will work in cross-functional teams, collaborating with experts across data science, engineering, strategy, design and consulting while gaining exposure to varied business challenges.

Optima provides an inclusive space for professional development, with a strong focus on continuous learning, mentoring and knowledge sharing. With the chance to work alongside experienced data scientists, engineers, analysts and product specialists, you will build practical skills in machine learning, statistics and experimentation while contributing to real client projects and developing a clear path for career progression.

What You Will Be Doing


Support the development and implementation of machine learning and statistical models to solve practical business problems.
Work with stakeholders to understand objectives, shape analytical approaches and communicate findings effectively.
Translate technical outputs into clear, transparent and actionable recommendations to support decision-making.
Explore data, test hypotheses and identify opportunities to create customer and commercial value.
Collaborate with teams across data science, engineering, strategy and design to deliver high-quality outcomes.
Support experimentation, model validation and performance monitoring to ensure analytical outputs deliver measurable impact.
Keep up to date with emerging data science techniques, including practical applications of Large Language Models.


What Skills We Would Like You To Have


Strong academic background in mathematics, statistics, science, engineering or another numerate discipline.
Minimum 2:1 degree in a STEM subject, with a postgraduate qualification in a quantitative field considered beneficial.
Good knowledge of statistics, including experimental design, uncertainty quantification and predictive modelling.
Some exposure to supervised and unsupervised machine learning techniques through commercial work, internships, training, personal projects or academic experience.
Proficiency in Python and/or R, with a willingness to develop deeper capability in operationalising data science solutions.
Ability to communicate complex analysis clearly to audiences with both technical and non-technical backgrounds.
Awareness of commercial value drivers such as revenue, cost, profitability and customer behaviour is advantageous.
Up to one year of commercial experience in data science, analytics, consulting or a related technical role; internships, placements, graduate schemes, bootcamps or strong project experience will also be considered.
Some exposure to working in a team environment, client-facing environment or on collaborative technical projects is desirable.
Awareness of Agile or Scrum ways of working is beneficial but not essential.


What You Will Bring


Strong problem-solving and analytical thinking abilities.
An inquisitive mindset, with curiosity about data, customer behaviour and commercial outcomes.
Good communication skills, with the ability to ask clear questions, share progress and explain technical ideas in an accessible way.
A team-oriented mindset with adaptability, independence and a willingness to learn from feedback.


This is an exciting opportunity to work directly on client projects, building practical data science capability while learning from experienced colleagues in a specialist data and AI consultancy.

What We Offer


Competitive base salary.
Inclusion in our annual discretionary bonus plan with an on-target performance bonus of up to 15%.
Up to 37 days holiday inclusive of personal and public allocations. Seven are fixed days for Christmas and New Year, and 30 are floating days taken at your discretion, subject to client scheduling and line manager approval.
Private medical insurance, single cover.
Group life and income protection insurance.
Salary sacrifice pension scheme after three months’ employment.
Access to over 1,000 perks and discounts via an employee discount portal.
Dedicated development time plus tools and funding to support personal and professional development.

Title: Senior Data Scientist
Description:
About Us

At Trainline, our purpose is to empower greener travel choices, connecting people and places. Trainline enables millions of travellers to find and book the best value tickets across carriers, fares, and journey options through our highly rated mobile app, website, and B2B partner channels.

Great journeys start with Trainline 🚄

We’re Europe’s leading independent rail platform, helping millions of travellers find and book the best-value rail and coach journeys across our app, website and partner channels.

Our job is to make the green travel choice the best choice. By building a better train travel experience, we help more people choose rail - creating a positive impact for customers, our business and the planet.

We’re a team of more than 1,000 Trainliners from over 50 nationalities, working across London, Paris, Barcelona, Milan, Edinburgh and Madrid. Now is a brilliant time to join us and help shape the future of travel.

Introducing the Trainline Data Science & Analytics Team 👋

Data Science & Analytics (DSA) sits at the heart of how Trainline understands and improves the end-to-end customer journey, from finding a journey through to booking. Our data scientists and analysts work closely together to support supply, search and commerce, spotting patterns that affect the customer experience, identifying opportunities for our customers and our business, and building solutions that make life easier for the wider team.

This role offers the chance to work across multiple areas of the business rather than being confined to a single specialism, giving you real breadth and the opportunity to see how different parts of the customer journey connect.

As a Senior Data Scientist, you will take ownership of investigations and solutions that span search, supply and commerce, working with detailed datasets and linking data sources to support projects across pillars. You will collaborate closely with all teams responsible for core customer experiences (from Data, Product, Engineering, Commercial), own problems and their solution end to end, challenge the status quo and help shape how the wider team approaches recurring problems and opportunities.

This is a role for someone who enjoys getting into the detail, thrives on variety, and wants to have a tangible impact on how customers experience Trainline.

In this role as the Senior Data Scientist, you will... 🚄


Work across search, supply and commerce, bringing together diverse datasets to tackle complex problems and deliver projects that span multiple pillars.
Identify opportunities for our customers and our business, using data to shape solutions and building tools and approaches that make the wider team more effective.
Develop a deep understanding of the customer experience, getting to the root causes of recurring problems (such as conversion declines, checkout errors or searches returning no results) and working cross-functionally to turn insights into lasting improvements.
Drive continuous improvement by identifying recurring patterns and turning what you learn into reusable tools, frameworks and solutions that reduce investigation time and help the wider team move faster.
Surface product and commercial opportunities through your analysis, connecting insights to business context and bringing opportunities to the right teams timely to drive action.
Mentor and guide colleagues across Data and partner teams, helping others build their analytical capability and confidence.
Partner closely with data scientists, data analysts and cross-functional teams across search, supply, commerce to solve problems that cut across organisational boundaries.
Navigate competing priorities across multiple areas of the business, bringing structure, clarity and sound judgement to fast-moving and ambiguous situations.


We'd love to hear from you if you have... 🔎


Substantial experience as a Data Scientist at a senior level, with the confidence, judgement and autonomy that come from having operated at this level before.
Track record of owning a business or functional area end to end, taking responsibility for identifying opportunities, shaping the analytical approach and driving outcomes - not just delivering analysis.
Experience working across multiple business areas or domains, navigating competing priorities and adapting your approach to different problems, stakeholders and contexts.
A strong track record of delivering measurable business impact through product analytics, translating data and insights into decisions and actions that improve customer and business outcomes.
Strong SQL and Python skills, used confidently to explore, analyse and draw actionable insights from complex datasets, alongside good engineering practices such as version control and effective use of AI tools to work more efficiently.
Confidence working with large, unfamiliar and diverse datasets, bringing together multiple data sources to build a robust and comprehensive understanding of a problem.
Experience mentoring and supporting other Data Scientists, helping colleagues develop their technical skills, analytical thinking and approach to problem-solving.
Ideally, experience in a technology-driven, digital or marketplace business, although this is not essential.


More Information

Enjoy fantastic perks like private healthcare & dental insurance, a generous work from abroad policy, 2-for-1 share purchase plans, an EV Scheme to further reduce carbon emissions, extra festive time off, and excellent family-friendly benefits.

We prioritise career growth with clear career paths, transparent pay bands, personal learning budgets, and regular learning days. Jump on board and supercharge your career from day one!

We're operating a hybrid model and ask that Trainliners work from the office a minimum of 60% of their time over a 12-week period. We also have a 28-day Work from Abroad policy.

Our Values Represent The Things That Matter Most To Us And What We Live And Breathe Everyday, In Everything We Do


💭 Think Big - We're building the future of rail
✔️ Own It - We focus on every customer, partner and journey
🤝 Travel Together - We're one team
♻️ Do Good - We make a positive impact


We know that having a diverse team makes us better and helps us succeed. And we mean all forms of diversity - gender, ethnicity, sexuality, disability, nationality and diversity of thought. That's why we're committed to creating inclusive places to work, where everyone belongs and differences are valued and celebrated.

Interested in finding out more about what it's like to work at Trainline? Why not check us out on LinkedIn, Instagram and Glassdoor!

Great journeys start with Trainline 🚄

We’re Europe’s leading independent rail platform, helping millions of travellers find and book the best-value rail and coach journeys across our app, website and partner channels.

Our job is to make the green travel choice the best choice. By building a better train travel experience, we help more people choose rail - creating a positive impact for customers, our business and the planet.

We’re a team of more than 1,000 Trainliners from over 50 nationalities, working across London, Paris, Barcelona, Milan, Edinburgh and Madrid. Now is a brilliant time to join us and help shape the future of travel.

Introducing the Trainline Data Science & Analytics Team 👋

Data Science & Analytics (DSA) sits at the heart of how Trainline understands and improves the end-to-end customer journey, from finding a journey through to booking. Our data scientists and analysts work closely together to support supply, search and commerce, spotting patterns that affect the customer experience, identifying opportunities for our customers and our business, and building solutions that make life easier for the wider team.

This role offers the chance to work across multiple areas of the business rather than being confined to a single specialism, giving you real breadth and the opportunity to see how different parts of the customer journey connect.

As a Senior Data Scientist, you will take ownership of investigations and solutions that span search, supply and commerce, working with detailed datasets and linking data sources to support projects across pillars. You will collaborate closely with all teams responsible for core customer experiences (from Data, Product, Engineering, Commercial), own problems and their solution end to end, challenge the status quo and help shape how the wider team approaches recurring problems and opportunities.

This is a role for someone who enjoys getting into the detail, thrives on variety, and wants to have a tangible impact on how customers experience Trainline.

In this role as the Senior Data Scientist, you will... 🚄

  • Work across search, supply and commerce, bringing together diverse datasets to tackle complex problems and deliver projects that span multiple pillars.
  • Identify opportunities for our customers and our business, using data to shape solutions and building tools and approaches that make the wider team more effective.
  • Develop a deep understanding of the customer experience, getting to the root causes of recurring problems (such as conversion declines, checkout errors or searches returning no results) and working cross-functionally to turn insights into lasting improvements.
  • Drive continuous improvement by identifying recurring patterns and turning what you learn into reusable tools, frameworks and solutions that reduce investigation time and help the wider team move faster.
  • Surface product and commercial opportunities through your analysis, connecting insights to business context and bringing opportunities to the right teams timely to drive action.
  • Mentor and guide colleagues across Data and partner teams, helping others build their analytical capability and confidence.
  • Partner closely with data scientists, data analysts and cross-functional teams across search, supply, commerce to solve problems that cut across organisational boundaries.
  • Navigate competing priorities across multiple areas of the business, bringing structure, clarity and sound judgement to fast-moving and ambiguous situations.

We'd love to hear from you if you have... 🔎

  • Substantial experience as a Data Scientist at a senior level, with the confidence, judgement and autonomy that come from having operated at this level before.
  • Track record of owning a business or functional area end to end, taking responsibility for identifying opportunities, shaping the analytical approach and driving outcomes - not just delivering analysis.
  • Experience working across multiple business areas or domains, navigating competing priorities and adapting your approach to different problems, stakeholders and contexts.
  • A strong track record of delivering measurable business impact through product analytics, translating data and insights into decisions and actions that improve customer and business outcomes.
  • Strong SQL and Python skills, used confidently to explore, analyse and draw actionable insights from complex datasets, alongside good engineering practices such as version control and effective use of AI tools to work more efficiently.
  • Confidence working with large, unfamiliar and diverse datasets, bringing together multiple data sources to build a robust and comprehensive understanding of a problem.
  • Experience mentoring and supporting other Data Scientists, helping colleagues develop their technical skills, analytical thinking and approach to problem-solving.
  • Ideally, experience in a technology-driven, digital or marketplace business, although this is not essential.

More Information

Enjoy fantastic perks like private healthcare & dental insurance, a generous work from abroad policy, 2-for-1 share purchase plans, an EV Scheme to further reduce carbon emissions, extra festive time off, and excellent family-friendly benefits.

We prioritise career growth with clear career paths, transparent pay bands, personal learning budgets, and regular learning days. Jump on board and supercharge your career from day one!

We're operating a hybrid model and ask that Trainliners work from the office a minimum of 60% of their time over a 12-week period. We also have a 28-day Work from Abroad policy.

Our Values Represent The Things That Matter Most To Us And What We Live And Breathe Everyday, In Everything We Do

  • 💭 Think Big - We're building the future of rail
  • ✔️ Own It - We focus on every customer, partner and journey
  • 🤝 Travel Together - We're one team
  • ♻️ Do Good - We make a positive impact

We know that having a diverse team makes us better and helps us succeed. And we mean all forms of diversity - gender, ethnicity, sexuality, disability, nationality and diversity of thought. That's why we're committed to creating inclusive places to work, where everyone belongs and differences are valued and celebrated.

Description:

Work with Us. Change the World.

Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our

services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of nearly 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

Job Description

About our Team

At AECOM, our team of air quality specialists delivers a range of exciting and varied projects across Europe, the Middle East and Africa. We work in multi-disciplinary teams delivering solutions to a broad base of client sectors including development, energy, oil and gas, water, government and transportation. The team now numbers more than 30 full-time air quality specialists in the UK and more than 500 practitioners worldwide.

This is a fantastic opportunity to kick start your career in air quality by gaining valuable work experience within an established consultancy. The role will involve working closely alongside experienced and senior members of the team assisting with air quality assessments for a variety of projects with local authorities, government, infrastructure providers, developers and industrial clients. Project involvement may include National Highways air quality assessments; air quality management studies for numerous local authorities; passive and continuous monitoring for the Silvertown Tunnel and HS2; and the development of emission inventories and digital tools.

Air Quality is part of AECOM’s Environment business which provides environmental management services for feasibility, impact analysis and operational compliance as well as remediation, restoration and re-use of impacted property.

Here's what you'll do:

Air quality monitoring; including site assessment, preparation and maintenance
Air quality dispersion modelling in combination with GIS
Data analysis and emissions inventory work
Air quality input into environmental statements
Assistance towards the coordination of multi-disciplinary project teams
Tender and proposal preparation


Enjoy the Perks

At AECOM, you'll enjoy a range of core and personalised benefits designed to support your future and well-being, customised to fit your lifestyle. Take advantage of career development opportunities, our flexible hybrid working model to ensure a work-life balance that suits your lifestyle, technical practice networks, AECOM University, and volunteering days.

Here is what you will get from us!

On the job support and learning

When a graduate starts at AECOM, we pair them with a member of the team who will guide and mentor them through their initial period working on live projects and business development tasks, to support with any technical queries.

Graduate Development Programme

Our 2-year graduate ADVANCE programme is designed to help you build your career in AECOM. You will attend several instructor-led training sessions where you will meet and hear from people across the business and take part in a series of interactive activities to equip you with the knowledge and skills you need to succeed in your role. Alongside the instructor-led elements of the ADVANCE programme, you will also engage with an online curriculum via AECOM University and can join the ADVANCE webinar series. We will provide you with all the support and tools you need to achieve your professional development ambitions, which may include Chartership with the relevant international professional institution.

We have more than 750 graduates on our programmes across the UK and Ireland from more than 40 different disciplines, each making a tangible difference to the environment in which we live and work.

The professional institute you will work towards is the Institute of Air Quality Management (IAQM).

See our digital early careers e-brochure here

Ready to push the limits of what’s possible?

ideally an MSc or PhD in Air Quality (Meteorology, Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, Environmental Engineering and Project Management and Climate Science, Environmental Management will be considered if there is an Air Quality focus )
Strong numeracy
Ability to communicate effectively to internal and external clients, both verbally & in writing with the confidence to engage with a variety of people (clients, colleagues, stakeholders and sub-contractors alike) and the aptitude to rationally explain, explore and discuss technical issues and capture feedback
Good Microsoft Office skills essential such as Word, Excel & PowerPoint
Ability to structure & prioritise work effectively through close cooperation and communication with the team as a whole
Strong attention to detail
Self-motivation, enthusiasm, hard working with ambition and drive
Excellent research and report writing skills
Ability to work in a team and independently without losing initiative & focus
Ability to work flexibly under pressure, responding to changing project and programme demands.


Preferred Qualifications

Awareness of GIS, modelling or programming skills would be an advantage

AECOM is the world’s trusted infrastructure consulting firm, delivering professional services throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. Title: Water Resources Planning Specialist
Description:
Joining ARUP




Arup’s purpose, shared values and collaborative approach has set us apart for 80 years, guiding how we shape a better world.




We work across the entire water cycle, with utilities, local and regional governments, commercial and domestic water users and other partners. From designing and maintaining key water infrastructure to advising on natural catchments and flood defences, we help clients to consider the long-term economic, environmental and social dimensions of their proposals.




The opportunity




We are seeking a Water Resources Planning Specialist to join our growing Water Resources team, supporting water companies to develop resilient, sustainable and evidence-based plans to meet future water needs.




Water resources planning is central to responding to climate change, population growth, environmental protection and long-term resilience. Working across Water Resource Management Plans, Drought Plans, regional planning studies and Strategic Resource Options, you will help clients make informed decisions about future water supplies, drought resilience and investment priorities.




This is primarily a technical specialist role, rather than a project management position. You will take ownership of defined technical work packages, working alongside specialists in hydrology, environmental assessment, economics, engineering and digital delivery to develop robust planning evidence and clear recommendations.




The Role Will Focus On




Water resources planning, strategy development and supply-demand balance assessment.
Drought resilience, adaptive planning and climate change scenario testing.
Water resources modelling, data analysis and interpretation of planning evidence.
Option appraisal, best-value planning and Strategic Resource Options.
Environmental and regulatory assessment, including SEA, HRA and WFD-related inputs.
Clear technical reporting, client workshops, consultations and regulatory submissions.




Is this role right for you?




If you have all or some of the skills and experience below, and a passion for making a difference in the water sector - we’d love to hear from you.




Experience in water resources planning, water company planning, hydrology, environmental assessment or a related discipline.
A degree, or equivalent experience, in water resources, civil engineering, environmental engineering, geography, environmental science, hydrology or a related subject.
Understanding of WRMPs, Drought Plans, supply-demand balance assessment and resilience planning.
Strong numerical, analytical and problem-solving skills, with experience analysing technical or environmental datasets.
Ability to prepare clear technical reports and communicate complex information simply.
Strong organisational skills, attention to detail and the ability to work collaboratively within multidisciplinary teams.




Desirable

Experience supporting SROs or regional planning studies.
Knowledge of water resources and drought planning guidance, including relevant methods and emerging issues.
Knowledge of climate change adaptation, adaptive planning, options appraisal or best-value planning.
Understanding of SEA, HRA or WFD.
Experience with GIS, spatial analysis, digital delivery, regulatory submissions or consultation.
Chartered status, or progress towards chartership, with CIWEM, ICE or another relevant institution.




You do not need to meet every requirement to apply. If you bring relevant experience, strong analytical skills and a willingness to keep learning, we would like to hear from you.




This role is intended for an established technical professional who is developing recognised expertise in water resources planning. You will lead defined technical work packages, provide high-quality planning advice and contribute to major water resources programmes, with support from senior specialists and project managers on overall project leadership and commercial management.




Please note, to ensure we remain GDPR compliant do not send your CV directly to us via this email.




What We Offer You




At Arup, we care about each member’s success, so we can grow together.




Guided by our values, we provide an attractive total reward package that recognises the contribution of each of our members to our shared success. As well as competitive, fair and equitable pay, we offer a career in which all of our members can belong, grow and thrive – through benefits that support health and wellbeing, a wide range of learning opportunities and many possibilities to have an impact through the work they do.




We are owned in trust on behalf of our members, giving us the freedom, with personal responsibility, to set our own direction and choose work that aligns with our purpose and adds to Arup’s legacy. Our members collaborate on ambitious projects to deliver remarkable outcomes for our clients and communities. Profit Share is a key part of our reward, enabling members to share in the results of our collective efforts.




We also provide Private medical insurance, Life assurance, Accident insurance and Income protection cover. In addition, you’ll have access to flexible benefits to help you look after all aspects of your wellbeing and give you the freedom and flexibility to find the best solutions for you, your family, and your individual needs.




Different people, shared values




Arup is an equal opportunity employer that actively promotes and nurtures a diverse and inclusive workforce. We welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds, regardless of age (within legal limits), gender identity or expression, marital status, disability, neurotype or mental health, race or ethnicity, faith or belief, sexual orientation, socioeconomic background, and whether you’re pregnant or on family leave. We are an open environment that embraces diverse experiences, perspectives, and ideas – this drives our excellence.




Guided by our values and alignment with the UN Sustainable Development Goals, we create and contribute to equitable spaces and systems, while cultivating a sense of belonging for all. Our internal employee networks support our inclusive culture: from race, ethnicity and cross-cultural working to gender equity and LGBTQ+ and disability inclusion – we aim to create a space for you to express yourself and make a positive difference. Discover more about life at Arup at www.arup.com/careers/your-life-at-arup




We are committed to making our recruitment process and workplaces accessible to all candidates. Please contact maria.mindrut@arup.com to let us know if you need any assistance or reasonable adjustments throughout your application or interview process, and/or to perform the essential functions of the role. We will do everything we can to support you.




Our Application Process




To understand what to expect next, please visit https://www.arup.com/careers/arup-careers-uk-application-process




Stay safe online – Arup will never ask for your bank details as part of our recruitment process.

Recruitment Agencies - We have a Preferred Supplier List of trusted partners to assist us when required and do not acknowledge any speculative CVs or unsolicited candidate introductions from agencies not on the list.

Title: AI First Engineer / Consultant
Description:
AI-First Engineering & Consultant 




Clear Rock AI | Remote-first, UK




** Instead of sending us a traditional PDF CV, create, link or upload an existing HTML click-through CV that demonstrates how you can use modern AI coding tools to generate slick UI that really sells your capability **

 

We’re building a different kind of technology consultancy: one where AI isn’t an add-on to the development process, it’s central to how problems are understood, software is built and organisations work.

 

We’re looking for a talented, curious software engineer who already works AI-first and wants to develop into an exceptional consultant. You don’t need to arrive as the finished article. We’re looking for strong engineering instincts, raw problem-solving ability, curiosity and the confidence to work with people. We’ll help you develop the consulting, facilitation and leadership skills around that.




What you'll be doing

 

You’ll work directly with clients on engagements taking real business and technology problems from ambiguity through to production.




That could include:

Turning business problems and desired outcomes into practical AI-driven solutions
Building applications, integrations and agentic workflows using LLMs and APIs
Using tools such as Claude Code, Codex and Cursor as a fundamental part of your engineering workflow
Taking products from customer concept through architecture, build, testing and production deployment
Helping teams tackle engineering problems such as refactoring, technical debt and modernisation using AI-first approaches
Rapidly understanding unfamiliar systems and codebases
Working with stakeholders to discover problems, explore options and communicate solutions
Helping client engineers adopt new tools and ways of working
Over time, developing the skills to facilitate workshops, coach teams, lead workstreams and advise senior stakeholders




Our aim is to help organisations move beyond individuals simply using AI to work faster, towards using AI-first development to solve bigger and more complex problems.




What we're looking for:

 

You’ll be a strong software engineer who:

Uses modern AI development tools every day, particularly Claude Code, Codex or Cursor
Has practical experience building software using LLMs, APIs and agentic workflows
Can take an unclear problem, break it down and turn it into a working solution
Has sound software engineering and architectural judgement
Is comfortable learning unfamiliar technologies and domains quickly
Is naturally curious about new technology and actively experiments with it
Communicates clearly with both technical and non-technical people
Is engaging, enthusiastic and able to bring people with you
Wants to develop beyond engineering into consulting, coaching and leadership




Must have: hands-on experience building AI-enabled software.




We care more about what you can build, how you think and how quickly you learn than a specific technology stack or number of years’ experience.




Salary: £80k




Hiring Process




Introductory conversation
Practical AI engineering challenge
Discussion of your solution, how you approached the problem and how you used AI




The challenge isn’t designed to test obscure technical knowledge. We want to understand how you solve problems, use AI as an engineering tool, make technical decisions and explain your thinking.

Title: AWS Data Engineer (Ref: 197894)
Description:
about the role


About Us

Forsyth Barnes is partnering with a market-leading technology business undertaking a major Analytics & AI transformation programme.

As part of a strategic move from a large on-premise estate to a modern AWS-based analytics platform, our client is investing heavily in cloud-native data capabilities that will power enterprise reporting, customer analytics, AI initiatives and future data products.

This is an opportunity to join a high-impact programme and help shape the future of data architecture across the organisation.

Job Description

We are looking for a Senior AWS Data Engineer to play a key role in designing, building and scaling a modern AWS data platform.

This is a hands-on engineering position requiring someone who has previously delivered cloud data platform initiatives and can combine technical leadership with practical delivery. You'll be responsible for helping move data from a large on-premise environment into AWS whilst establishing scalable ingestion frameworks, reusable data products and event-driven data capabilities.

The successful candidate will be comfortable mentoring engineers, challenging technical decisions and contributing directly to the build and ongoing evolution of the platform.

Key Responsibilities


Design, build and optimise AWS-native data pipelines and cloud data platform capabilities.
Deliver ingestion solutions using CDC, event-driven and batch processing patterns.
Build scalable ETL/ELT frameworks and reusable data products using Python and SQL.
Support migration of data from a large on-premise estate into AWS.
Design and implement robust data models supporting analytics and reporting requirements.
Develop data quality, observability, governance and monitoring frameworks.
Collaborate closely with Architects, Engineers, Data Scientists and Product teams.
Provide technical leadership and mentoring whilst remaining hands-on.
Support performance optimisation, cloud cost management and operational excellence initiatives.


Requirements


Proven commercial experience as an AWS Data Engineer or Data Platform Engineer.
Strong experience working with AWS services including S3, Glue, Athena, EMR and Lambda.
Advanced SQL and Python skills.
Strong data modelling expertise, including dimensional modelling and analytics-ready data design.
Experience delivering end-to-end cloud data platforms from ingestion through to consumption.
Ability to lead and mentor engineers whilst remaining hands-on technically.
Strong understanding of modern Data Engineering principles and best practices.


Desirable


Change Data Capture (CDC) experience.
AWS DMS experience.
Event-driven architecture experience.
Kafka and/or Flink.
Apache Iceberg.
dbt and Airflow.
Lakehouse architectures and Medallion modelling.
FinOps, observability and cost optimisation.
Terraform and Infrastructure as Code.


Benefits


Meaningful ownership of cloud data engineering work that supports transportation, logistics and digitally enabled services.
Technical scope across ingestion, lakehouse design, governance, data products and AWS platform optimisation rather than a narrowly defined pipeline remit.
Exposure to analytics, machine learning and emerging AI initiatives as the organisation expands its data capabilities.
Opportunity to influence reusable engineering standards, delivery patterns and the practical adoption of data-product principles.
Collaboration with architecture, platform, software, product and analytical professionals across a varied technology landscape.
Access to a role where strong engineering decisions can improve reliability, insight and operational performance at scale.
Professional growth through hands-on work with modern AWS services, contemporary data practices and complex integration challenges.
A competitive package aligned with the responsibilities and experience required for this position.


Other

The position is based in Nottingham, England, and is suited to an engineer who combines strong AWS delivery skills with an interest in platform design and business outcomes. Experience from transportation, logistics, software, telecommunications or another data-intensive sector will transfer well.

Applicants should be prepared to demonstrate how they have improved the reliability, usability or governance of production data platforms. The successful candidate will bring curiosity, practical judgement and the ability to turn evolving requirements into robust engineering outcomes.

Title: Academy Head of Performance Analysis
Company: The Association of Professional Football Analysis
Description:
Full Time Nottingham, UK Posted on September 13, 2026 Closes: September 19, 2026

Nottingham Forest Football Club is recruiting an Academy Head of Performance Analysis to lead, coordinate and drive the delivery of performance analysis support across all Academy age groups. Based at the Nigel Doughty Academy and reporting to the Assistant Academy Manager, the successful candidate will manage the day-to-day operations of the Academy analysis department, track player development through objective and subjective performance data, and help embed the Academy's philosophy and methodology across the development pathway.

Responsibilities


Lead the support provision and requirements of the performance analysis function within the Academy.
Oversee the analysis related to philosophy and methodology, aiding the Academy vision.
Manage day-to-day Academy analysis operations, ensuring effective processes deliver actionable insights across all age groups.
Work in partnership with MDT teams to ensure high-level reporting is delivered to players, coaches and key stakeholders across the Academy and loans.
Oversee individual analysis of Academy players using subjective and objective data to inform the Head of Academy and Academy Management Team.
Lead specific analysis projects related to the long-term development of the Nottingham Forest Academy analysis department.
Drive the club's analytical products and processes to deliver high-quality insights that support player development and performance outcomes.
Ensure an effective professional development programme is implemented for individual staff and the analysis team.
Recruit permanent staff when the need arises, in line with club protocols.
Manage and oversee the Academy internship programme, supporting the recruitment, development and day-to-day guidance of interns within the department.
Produce monthly, quarterly and yearly reports in line with the Academy strategy, updating on progress against the performance analysis strategic pillar.
Build successful and professional relationships with players and staff while maintaining professional distance from playing staff at all times.


Experience, Skills & Qualifications


Excellent understanding of football tactics and talent identification in players.
Educated in Performance Analysis, Sports Science and/or coaching, and holding a UEFA B Licence.
Full knowledge and experience of all duties involved in a role of this nature.
Excellent attention to detail, highly organised and punctual.
Able to communicate effectively at all levels, with strong verbal and written communication skills.
Works effectively in a fast-paced environment, remaining calm under pressure and comfortable with tight deadlines.
Drive to achieve deadlines, prioritise workload effectively and continually improve efficiency and effectiveness.
Excellent interpersonal skills with people of all ages and backgrounds, able to maintain confidentiality and act with tact and diplomacy.
Excellent IT skills, including MS Office, intranets, web and Outlook.
Experience in health and safety duties appropriate to the post (desirable).
Prior experience managing kit and equipment within a sporting institution, preferably football (desirable).


Location: The Nigel Doughty Academy, Nottingham, NG2 7SR

Contract: Full Time, 42 hours per week

Department: Academy — reporting to the Assistant Academy Manager

The successful applicant may be required to undergo a DBS check as part of the club's commitment to safeguarding. Nottingham Forest Football Club is an equal opportunities employer and a Disability Confident Committed employer.

Title: Market Insight and Research Lead
Description:
Job Title: Market Research Lead

Function: Strategy & Business Architecture

Location: Hybrid Worker – Expectation is two days per week on site at our Nottingham office

Contract type: Permanent

Salary: Offered on a starting salary of £65,920 with the potential to increase to £77,553 over the course of three years. Plus, a car allowance of £7000 per anum.

Closing Date: Thursday 15th October 2026

NHS Supply Chain currently has an opportunity for a Market Research Lead to join our team during an exciting period of transformation, working to make it easier for the NHS to put patients first.

We are looking for an experienced and strategic Market Research Lead to help shape the future of NHS Supply Chain through powerful insight, evidence-based decision making, and a deep understanding of customer and stakeholder needs. This is an exciting opportunity to lead the organisation's research and insight agenda, ensuring the voice of customers, stakeholders and the wider healthcare system is embedded in strategic thinking and business planning. You will play a crucial role in identifying opportunities for improvement, measuring impact, and turning complex findings into meaningful actions that enhance performance across the organisation. Leading a team of two Market Researchers, you will champion research excellence, innovation and continuous improvement, while ensuring the business has access to clear, actionable insight that drives better outcomes for customers, patients and the NHS

Every day you will … 


Lead and evolve our research and insight strategy, ensuring stakeholder and customer perspectives inform key business decisions.
Be the organisational expert for customer satisfaction (CSAT) and stakeholder experience measurement, embedding best practice approaches that provide a true and trusted view of performance.
Design and oversee high-quality quantitative and qualitative research programmes that generate robust, actionable insights.
Monitor emerging trends across healthcare, procurement, customer experience and stakeholder needs, translating findings into strategic recommendations.
Work closely with senior leaders and stakeholders across the business to identify research priorities and evaluate the impact of improvement initiatives.
Develop engaging dashboards, reports and presentations that bring data and insight to life for audiences at every level.
Foster a culture of evidence-based decision making, ensuring insight drives action and measurable outcomes.
Lead, coach and develop a team of Market Researchers, creating a high-performing and collaborative environment.
Establish and maintain research governance, quality standards and best practice methodologies across the organisation.
Build and nurture a vibrant research community that encourages innovation, knowledge sharing and continuous learning.


 

What can we offer you?

We Want To Reward You For Your Passion, Enthusiasm, And Hard Work So We Offer Much More Than a Competitive Salary


Hybrid working opportunities, giving you the flexibility to work collaboratively in the office and remotely.  
We recognise our employees' hard work and contributions with annual bonus schemes, long service, and colleague recognition awards. 
27 days holiday plus bank holidays
We are dedicated to your development, through in-house training, support, and access to external qualifications to maximise your potential.
A focus on your well-being offering 1 day of paid well-being leave and free access to the 24/7 Employee Assistance Programme
Generous pension scheme (with us contributing 12% when you contribute 6%)
Access to our Flexible Benefits Scheme, where you can choose from a variety of benefits such as Life Insurance, Critical Illness Cover, Income Protection, Health Cash Plan, Dental Insurance, and additional pension contributions that suit you.
2 days of paid volunteering leave allowing you to give back to your community. 
Access to many discounts from the Blue Light Card to NHS Discounts.


 

NHS Supply Chain, who are we?

Our role is to support the NHS to save lives and improve health. We are a part of the NHS family, and our role is to source, deliver and supply healthcare products, services and food for NHS trusts and healthcare organisations across England and Wales.

 

We serve every NHS Trust and operate a national network of distribution centres, managing relationships with more than a thousand suppliers and delivering more than 8,000,000 orders each year to more than 17,000 locations. Doing all of this on behalf of the NHS gives NHS staff more time to focus on their main priority of providing excellent patient care.

 

What skills will help you thrive in this role?


Significant experience leading market research, customer insight or stakeholder research programmes.
A strong understanding of quantitative and qualitative research methodologies and their practical application.
Experience translating complex data and research findings into compelling business recommendations.
A proven ability to influence stakeholders and drive organisational change through evidence and insight.
Experience presenting findings and recommendations to senior leaders and executive audiences.
Strong leadership skills with experience developing, coaching and motivating teams.
Excellent communication and storytelling skills, with the ability to make insight accessible and actionable.
Knowledge of customer satisfaction, stakeholder experience and performance measurement frameworks.
An interest in healthcare, public sector research, or complex stakeholder environments would be advantageous.


Our Inclusive Commitment

At NHS Supply Chain, we are committed to building an inclusive environment where difference is not only valued, but celebrated, giving everyone the opportunity to thrive in their career. Developing our people is key to our success, so if this role sounds like the right next step in your career but your experience doesn’t match perfectly with the job advert, we encourage you to still apply.

Struggling to complete our application form, and require additional support? Reach out to our Talent Acquisition team at careers@supplychain.nhs.uk who will be happy to help you with alternative ways to apply.

We reserve the right to close any vacancy from further submissions when we have received sufficient applications from which to make a shortlist. Please apply without delay if you wish to be considered for this role.

Title: Finance Business Partner
Description:
Alexander Daniels is partnering with a successful manufacturing business to recruit a Finance Business Partner for a newly enhanced position with a strong focus on data, ERP systems, reporting automation and manufacturing analytics.




This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys getting into the detail, improving processes and creating meaningful reporting that drives operational performance.




Working closely with Finance, Operations and Commercial teams, you will play a pivotal role in transforming the quality of reporting and business insight across the organisation. This is not a traditional management accounting or business partnering role. The successful individual will be heavily involved in developing automated reporting, improving ERP utilisation, enhancing data quality and building robust manufacturing costing models.




The Role

Key responsibilities will include:

Developing and maintaining manufacturing costing models and margin analysis.
Improving ERP system utilisation and reporting functionality.
Designing and automating operational and financial reporting.
Creating dashboards, KPIs and management information to support decision-making.
Analysing production performance, machine utilisation, labour efficiency and downtime data.
Identifying opportunities to improve data quality, reporting accuracy and business processes.
Acting as a key link between Finance, Operations and IT.
Supporting commercial decision-making through robust financial and operational analysis.
Driving continuous improvement across systems, processes and reporting frameworks.




About You

We are keen to speak with individuals who can demonstrate:

Experience within a manufacturing environment.
Strong costing and manufacturing finance knowledge.
Proven experience working with ERP systems.
Advanced Excel skills and a passion for reporting and analytics.
Experience developing automated reporting solutions.
Exposure to Power BI, SQL or similar business intelligence tools would be advantageous.
A hands-on approach with a willingness to challenge existing processes and improve efficiency.
The ability to translate complex data into meaningful business insight.




The Opportunity

This role offers the chance to join a growing business where you can make a genuine impact. You'll be given the autonomy to improve reporting, influence decision-making and help shape how operational and financial data is utilised across the organisation.




It's ideally suited to a commercially minded finance professional who enjoys the technical and analytical side of the role as much as partnering with stakeholders.

Title: AI & Automation Solution Consultant
Description:
Company Description

Experian is a global data and technology company, powering opportunities for people and businesses around the world. We operate across a range of markets, from financial services to healthcare, automotive, agribusiness, insurance, and many more. Experian invests in people and new advanced technologies to unlock the power of data. We have an amazing team of 25,200 people in 32 countries.

Job Description

The AI & Automation Centre of Expertise (GenAI CoE) at Experian helps teams across Experian's UK business. It improves products using Generative AI, machine learning, and automation. The centre has a focus on responsible, measurable impact.

This is a hybrid role reporting into the Head of Automation for someone who enjoys both shaping ideas and bringing them to life.

You'll Work Across Two Connected Areas


Opportunity discovery and product ownership: identifying, refining, and validating AI and automation use cases
Prototyping and technical scoping: building and testing solutions using low-code tools and latest technologies


An important part of your role is the ability to switch between focusing on pipeline and opportunity shaping, into hands-on delivery to remove bottlenecks and accelerate progress.

Who are we looking for?

Someone Who Is


Comfortable working with early-stage, ambiguous ideas and turning them into structured opportunities
Hands-on and curious, with an interest in testing and building solutions quickly
Motivated by learning— new AI capabilities and low-code tools as they emerge
You will connect needs, data, and technology to make better decisions


A big part of the job is choosing the right approach — when AI is valuable, and when simpler analytics or Automation is the better answer. This is not a pure developer role, and not a traditional product owner role. It sits between both—focused on turning ideas into tangible outcomes.

What You'll Do


Work with partners to translate business problems into clearly defined user cases
Build and manage a pipeline of AI and automation opportunities
Assess feasibility, value and suitability of AI vs traditional approaches
Scope solutions, defining MVP, success criteria and experimentation approaches
Develop rapid prototypes and MVPs using low-code / no-code platforms
Communicate outcomes, including trade-offs, risks, and recommendations
Explore and apply new tools to improve how we deliver


Qualifications


Experience in a product, digital, or technical role where you have shaped and delivered solutions
Experience communicating product benefits appropriate for each prospect, with experience working across business and technical partners
You will have experience translating business problems into structured use cases and deliverable solutions
Comfortable working in uncertain or exploratory environments, using experimentation to guide progress
A curiosity for AI and automation, and an interest in how they are applied in real-world settings


It would be great if you also have


Exposure to AI use cases such as generative AI, classification, or workflow automation
Experience running experiments, pilots, or MVP-style delivery
Experience with low-code / no-code platforms
Experience explaining technical concepts or analysis to non-technical partners


Additional Information

Benefits package includes:


Hybrid working - 40% office based
Great compensation package and discretionary bonus plan
Core benefits include pension, bupa healthcare, sharesave scheme and more!
25 days annual leave with 8 bank holidays and 3 volunteering days. You can also purchase additional annual leave.


Internal Grade D/EB8

Our uniqueness is that we celebrate yours. Experian's people first, inclusive and purpose driven culture is multi award-winning; World's Best Workplaces™ 2025 (Fortune Global Top 25), Great Place To Work™ in 26 countries to name a few. Check out Experian Life on social or explore our Careers Site to understand why. Experian is also proud to be an Equal Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer. Title: Senior Complaints Insight Specialist
Description:
Nottingham Trent House (95002), United Kingdom, Nottingham, Nottinghamshire

Senior Complaints Insight Specialist

About The Role

We are looking for a Senior Complaints Insight Specialist to join our Complaints Process & Insight team on a permanent basis. In this role, you will help us use customer complaints as a driving force for change, translating deep insights into strategic opportunities for investment.

As part of a specialist team of six, you will collaborate across the organisation, particularly within our Operations department to deliver data-driven customer insights and enhance our complaints strategy. Reporting directly to the Head of Complaints Strategy, you will leverage data to spot patterns, identify why things go wrong, and create compelling visual narratives for stakeholders at all levels . While you will possess strong analytical capabilities to partner with our centralised Data Analysts, this is a highly collaborative role focused on turning data into impactful business actions.

What you'll do


Lead Insight Projects: Initiate and manage complaints insight initiatives from problem-solving through to successful implementation alongside internal stakeholders.
Trend Identification: Partner with the UK Customer Operations management team to identify real-time dissatisfaction trends and drive initiatives that improve customer outcomes and operational efficiency.
Strategy & Risk Management: Manage and enhance the complaints strategy, including associated risks and process controls, while maintaining clear communication with internal partners.
Stakeholder Storytelling: Prepare and deliver concise, compelling written reports and presentations that translate complex data into actionable recommendations for the business.
Regulatory Reporting & Analysis: Leverage internal, industry, and Financial Ombudsman Service (FOS) data to uncover root causes, while collaborating globally to deliver key regulatory reports.


Essential

The skills and experience you need


Data Storytelling & Visualisation: Exceptional ability to build engaging presentations and use data visualisation to turn complex numbers into simple, compelling narratives.
Analytical Expertise: Strong experience using both qualitative and quantitative analytical methods to evaluate large datasets and find root causes.
Collaboration & Interpersonal Skills: A proven track record of fostering teamwork and collaborating effectively across diverse disciplines and organisational levels.
Strategy & Process Improvement: Detail-oriented mindset with hands-on experience in strategy design, process management, and delivering sustainable operational improvements.
Creative Problem Solving: An outside-the-box thinker who can cut through complexity to deliver straightforward, actionable solutions.


Desirable


Regulated Environment Experience: Prior experience working within a regulated complaints handling environment.
Digital Tools: Proficiency with collaborative tools, specifically Google Workspace (including Google Sheets and Google Slides).


Where and how you'll work

This is a permanent position based in our Nottingham office.

We embrace a hybrid approach to work. You'll spend three days a week in the office (Tuesday-Thursday), with Monday and Friday being dedicated work-from-home days.

Our offices are designed to inspire and support you. At our Nottingham head office, you'll find an on-site gym, restaurant and dedicated Learning Loft. Our London office boasts a rooftop running track and coffee bar.

What’s in it for you

We invest in the growth of our people alongside our business. You will have extensive opportunities to learn and develop your career, including access to up to £5,000 in funding for external qualifications.

Benefits

In addition to career development, our comprehensive benefits package is designed to grow with you, ensuring your wellbeing is prioritised at every stage of your career:


Wealth & Future: Competitive pension and performance-based bonus schemes
Holidays: Start with 25 days of annual leave, increasing with tenure. Need more? You have the option to buy 5 additional days.
Health: Access premium care through our private medical insurance.
Family Support: We champion your milestones with enhanced parental leave.


A full list of our benefits is available here.

What You Should Know About How We Recruit

We pride ourselves on hiring the best people, not the same people. Building diverse and inclusive teams is the right thing to do and the smart thing to do. We want to work with top talent: whoever you are, whatever you look like, wherever you come from. We know it’s about what you do, not just what you say. That’s why we make our recruitment process fair and accessible.

We value diversity, inclusion and belonging at our core. We empower our associates to do great work by creating an inclusive culture—one that values diverse perspectives, fosters collaboration and encourages innovative ideas—and a place where associates of all backgrounds can thrive by bringing their most authentic selves to work. We call this our Culture of Belonging, and it rests at the heart of our business.

Our associate-led Business Resource Groups were created to help support our diverse population and include over 10 groups across our offices. Because each Business Resource Group is as unique as the population it serves, they offer a range of activities, networking opportunities, special events and learning programmes to associates.

Capital One is committed to diversity in the workplace.

If you require a reasonable adjustment, please contact ukrecruitment@capitalone.com All information will be kept confidential and will only be used for the purpose of applying a reasonable adjustment.

For technical support or questions about Capital One's recruiting process, please send an email to Careers@capitalone.com

Capital One does not provide, endorse nor guarantee and is not liable for third-party products, services, educational tools or other information available through this site.

Capital One Financial is made up of several different entities. Please note that any position posted in Canada is for Capital One Canada, any position posted in the United Kingdom is for Capital One Europe and any position posted in the Philippines is for Capital One Philippines Service Corp. (COPSSC).

Who We Are

At Capital One, we're building a leading information-based technology company. Still founder-led by Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Richard Fairbank, Capital One is on a mission to help our customers succeed by bringing ingenuity, simplicity, and humanity to banking. We measure our efforts by the success our customers enjoy and the advocacy they exhibit. We are succeeding because they are succeeding.

Guided by our shared values, we thrive in an environment where collaboration and openness are valued. We believe that innovation is powered by perspective and that teamwork and respect for each other lead to superior results. We elevate each other and obsess about doing the right thing. Our associates serve with humility and a deep respect for their responsibility in helping our customers achieve their goals and realize their dreams. Together, we are on a quest to change banking for good.

Title: Engineering Graduate Programme (Nottingham)
Description:
Programme start date: September 2027

Are you passionate about engineering and technology?

Do you want to make a difference by delivering software used by some of the biggest companies in the world?

Do you thrive in dynamic, agile environments and enjoy collaborating with others?

Eligibility Criteria:


To be eligible you must be a final year undergraduate or Masters student in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Engineering, Information Technology or related discipline and have completed all the requirements of your course before August/September 2027 or a fresh graduate in class of 2026.


Highlights of the Graduate Programme


Progress through a 12-month development journey aiming to build foundational skills that are key for your future success
Build your foundational knowledge of LSEG, Financial Markets and the business during your global induction
'Engineering Bootcamp' week to immerse you in the business and Engineering principles
Participate in group projects which are aligned to LSEG goals
Meet in person with your cohort at ‘Ignite’, the programme mid-point skills offsite. Explore key knowledge areas and skills
Access opportunities to earn industry-recognized qualifications, including 5 study days during programme
Connect with global early careers community and opportunities and contribute to wider society via CSR initiatives and volunteering opportunities 


After completing the programme, graduates transition into permanent roles within Engineering, aligned with their interests and business needs.

Engineering

Roles in the Engineering apply deep technical and analytical expertise to build, operate and improve the platforms, products, services and models that power our business. Spanning software and platform, reliability, quality, cyber security, service operations, service management, financial engineering and data science, these roles work across the full lifecycle to solve complex problems, enable secure and resilient delivery, and drive continuous improvement in a product-led, data-driven environment. 

Job Families

Software & Platform Engineering

Roles in Software & Platform Engineering focus on building and improving the software, infrastructure and systems that support our products and services. Engineers work across the full software and infrastructure lifecycle to deliver usable, maintainable applications.

Reliability Engineering

Roles in the Reliability Engineering track play a crucial role in identifying and reducing risks to performance and availability. They develop tools and implement strategies to prevent problems before they occur and recover quickly from a failure keeping platforms, applications, and services stable and reliable.

What We Are Looking For

We are passionate about recruiting people who have a genuine curiosity about Technology and strive to pursue a Technology career path, as evidenced by their studies, extracurriculars or work experience. It’s important to us that you can also understand the breadth of our organisation, how it functions and the vital role that technology plays in supporting LSEG and our clients.


You will have a strong interest in technology proven either via your work experience, extracurricular activities, or academic studies. For instance, you may have secured an internship in a technology role or focused on technology as part of a university project. You may have learnt how to code or how to use a particular technology.
You should have a demonstrable interest in financial markets, which you’ve built through your studies, work experience or extracurricular activities.
A curiosity for data and an ability to analyse information to draw conclusions and propose solutions.
Individuals who can connect the dots and think strategically.
The environment we work in is fast paced, you’ll need to demonstrate focus, resilience and the flexibility to adapt to changing demands.
People who can collaborate with others, using their communication skills in the process.
Ideal candidates will have the rights to work in the UK without restrictions.


We value not just what you achieve, but how you achieve it.

We are considering candidates beyond the core software degrees (e.g. computer science, software engineering, Mathematics and Informatics) and candidate with physics, engineering, electronic degree who can demonstrate an interest in Technology as evidenced by extracurriculars or work experience, or personal projects can apply.

Application close: 16th November, however we recommend an early application because we consider candidates on a rolling basis. Due to the volume of applications, we might close the applications earlier, so we recommend an early application.  

Recruitment Process:

The first stage of the recruitment process involves making an application and submitting your resume. The second stage is completing Technical and Coding Assessment. The third stage of the application process is an Immersive Online Assessment. The assessment is designed to give you an insight into what it’s like to work at LSEG The fourth stage is a video interview where you will answer a series of questions using a strength-based-interview style The final stage is a half day assessment centre which involves several different types of exercises – further information is provided at the point of invite.

  

Please review all the graduate programme opportunities and make one application If you make more than one application, we will review your first application only.

Please note, all our assessment centres are held virtually.

Life at LSEG

At LSEG, we provide our employees with a comprehensive benefits portfolio as part of a competitive total rewards package. Our benefit plans are designed to supplement the financial, emotional and physical wellbeing of our employees and their families at all stages of their life. We encourage an appreciative, collaborative and inclusive culture that promotes employee and organisational wellbeing.

We believe hybrid working makes more possible and recognise difference as a good thing. We want to set everyone up to bring their best self to work. Everyone will spend time with colleagues in the office, but you’ll be trusted to work flexibly, in a way that delivers excellence.  

Career Stage:

Associate

London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG) Information:

Join us and be part of a team that values innovation, quality, and continuous improvement. If you're ready to take your career to the next level and make a significant impact, we'd love to hear from you.

LSEG is a leading global financial markets infrastructure and data provider. Our purpose is driving financial stability, empowering economies and enabling customers to create sustainable growth.

Our purpose is the foundation on which our culture is built. Our values of Integrity, Partnership, Excellence and Change underpin our purpose and set the standard for everything we do, every day. They go to the heart of who we are and guide our decision making and everyday actions.

Working with us means that you will be part of a dynamic organisation of 25,000 people across 65 countries. However, we will value your individuality and enable you to bring your true self to work so you can help enrich our diverse workforce.

We are proud to be an equal opportunities employer. This means that we do not discriminate on the basis of anyone’s race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, marital status, veteran status, pregnancy or disability, or any other basis protected under applicable law. Conforming with applicable law, we can reasonably accommodate applicants' and employees' religious practices and beliefs, as well as mental health or physical disability needs.

You will be part of a collaborative and creative culture where we encourage new ideas. We are committed to sustainability across our global business and we are proud to partner with our customers to help them meet their sustainability objectives. Our charity, the LSEG Foundation provides charitable grants to community groups that help people access economic opportunities and build a secure future with financial independence. Colleagues can get involved through fundraising and volunteering.

Title: KTP Research Associate in Mathematics Learning (Fixed Term)
Description:
Area

Psychology

Location

UK Other

Salary

£35,000 to £48,000 per annum, depending on skills and experience.

Closing Date

Friday 09 October 2026

Reference

SCI1664626

The University of Nottingham invites applications for a KTP Research Associate (Mathematics Learning) to join a unique collaboration with Maths Circle, the team behind Times Tables Rock Stars and NumBots. This is an opportunity to carry out rigorous applied research in a fast-moving EdTech environment, and to see your findings translate directly into product changes that can improve the experience of maths learning for children at scale.

Maths Circle’s ambition is simple: to help every child confidently say, “I am good at maths.”

Supported by academics within the University of Nottingham’s Human Development and Learning Research Group and Loughborough University’s Centre for Mathematical Cognition, you will lead a high-profile Knowledge Transfer Partnership exploring how psychological factors such as maths anxiety, attitudes and self-concept influence engagement and learning.

Why this role is different

What makes this role unusual is the closeness between research and implementation. You will not simply produce findings and hand them over. You will work alongside researchers, product teams, designers and engineers to turn evidence into practical changes, then help evaluate whether those changes improve engagement, confidence and learning outcomes. Based at Maths Circle in Bedford, your research could directly influence how questions are sequenced, how learners are supported when they disengage, the impact of confidence or anxiety, and what insights teachers receive about the children in their class.

You will have the opportunity to work with rich, large-scale learner data alongside newly collected psychological and qualitative data, creating a rare opportunity to connect what children do, how they feel, and how they learn.

You will have:


A PhD (or close to completion) in Cognitive Development, Mathematical Cognition, Mathematics Education or a closely related discipline.
Knowledge and experience of a range of research methods and designs.
Excellent advanced data analysis skills of large data sets.
Experience carrying out research with child participants.
Experience working in or with primary schools and understanding of the education sector.
Ability to manage projects effectively and communicate progress clearly with colleagues and stakeholders.
Prior industrial experience or commercial awareness are desirable.


This exciting opportunity is funded through a Knowledge Transfer Partnership (KTP). KTP is a UK Government scheme promoting mutually beneficial relationships between universities and industry. You will have your own budget (£2,000 pa) for training and CPD, helping you develop your skillset and reach your personal/professional career goals. 

We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds and experiences. We value different working styles and can offer reasonable adjustments during recruitment and in the workplace.

This is a fixed-term position for 24 months, working full-time at 35 hours per week.

Informal enquiries may be addressed to Lucy Cragg, email address: lucy.cragg@nottingham.ac.uk. Please note that applications sent to this address will not be accepted.

Travel expenses for interviews cannot be reimbursed for this position.

It is a condition of this post that satisfactory enhanced disclosure is obtained from the 'Disclosure and Barring Service'.

Title: Research Associate/ Fellow (Fixed Term)
Description:
Area

Veterinary Medicine & Science

Location

Sutton Bonington

Salary

£32,080 to £47,389 per annum, depending on skills and experience (minimum £35608 with relevant PhD).

Closing Date

Thursday 15 October 2026

Reference

MED2148626

We are seeking a highly motivated and enthusiastic Postdoctoral Research Fellow to join the molecular biology group led by Professor Victoria James at the University of Nottingham. This exciting position is funded by an Alzheimer's Research UK (ARUK) project awarded to Clinical Lead Dr Anto Rajamani and offers an opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge research aimed at improving the diagnosis of Dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB).

The successful candidate will deliver the experimental research focused on improving the diagnostic accuracy of a multiplex plasma extracellular vesicle (EV) RNA biomarker assay for DLB. This work has the potential to advance earlier and more accurate diagnosis of one of the most challenging neurodegenerative diseases.

The postholder will lead the generation and analysis of next-generation RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) data from patient-derived extracellular vesicle samples to identify DLB-specific RNA signatures. They will also support the implementation and evaluation of artificial intelligence (AI)-based analytical approaches to improve the sensitivity and specificity of biomarker-based diagnosis.

Working within a multidisciplinary and collaborative environment, you will work closely with our clinical lead, Dr Anto Rajamani, members of the molecular biology laboratory, PhD students, bioinformatics collaborators, and other clinical partners.

This position provides an outstanding opportunity to contribute to translational research with real potential to improve patient diagnosis and care. You will join a supportive and collaborative research environment within the University of Nottingham and work alongside leading researchers in molecular biology, clinical neurology, biomarker discovery, and computational analysis. You will play an important role in driving the project forward while contributing to the development of an inclusive, supportive, and collaborative research culture.

What the university offers:


A friendly, diverse, and supportive working environment
A hybrid working arrangement with the blended approach of home and office working
Generous holiday entitlement of 30 days (or pro rata) plus standard bank holidays and five university closure days including closure between Christmas and New Year
We are committed to staff development through the provision of training, continued support, and career progression opportunities
You will have access to a range of benefits and rewards, including fitness and health facilities, staff discounts, travel schemes and many more. To find out more about what we can offer you, follow the link to our benefits website


We are committed to fostering equality, diversity, and inclusion and welcome applications from candidates from all backgrounds. Flexible working arrangements and opportunities for career development are supported wherever possible.

If you are passionate about translational neuroscience, biomarker discovery, and applying innovative molecular and computational approaches to improve dementia diagnosis, we would be delighted to hear from you.

Further information is available in the role profile. This position is a fixed-term contract for 30 months. To apply for this vacancy please click ‘Apply Now’ to complete your details and upload a copy of your CV.

Please contact Professor Victoria James ( Victoria.james@nottingham.ac.uk ) and Dr Anto Rajamani ( Anto.Rajamani@nottingham.ac.uk ) if you have further questions about this role. Please note that we will be unable to accept applications sent directly by email.
